articles.title: Stephen Curry’s Thirty Ink generates $173 million as the NBA star expands business empire ahead of the new season
articles.summary: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, has proven his worth on the court as he remains one of the most reliable players in the league.
articles.body: Stephen Curry, the Golden State Warriors’ star player, has proven his worth on the court as he remains one of the most reliable players in the league. While Stephen Curry is gearing up for the new season with the team, he has also been a successful entrepreneur. Ahead of the new season, Stephen Curry’s brand conglomerate, Thirty Ink, has generated multi million dollars in profits.Stephen Curry’s company generates multi million dollars in profit as the four time NBA champion proves his business acumenAs per reports, in 2024, Stephen Curry’s Thirty Ink, a house of brands conglomerate that owns companies including Unanimous Media, Gentleman's Cut bourbon and Underrated Golf and Basketball, has generated $173.5 million in revenue and $144 million in EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization), with every single business unit operating profitably.In an interview with CNBC, Suresh Singh, the company's secretary chairman, reflected on the brand conglomerate, Thirty Ink’s success as he said, "It's completely unique," said Singh. "One of the big things, I believe, is that there's a lot of athlete- and celebrity-driven partnerships and businesses that aren't necessarily focused on profit, aren't necessarily focused on mission. We do both."Erick Peyton, the multimedia company's co-founder and co CEO along with Stephen Curry said, "He knows every single project on our slate, which is probably around 40 right now…His vision is to inspire through media. It's really a feeling when you watch our projects, hopefully you're a little bit happier, you know, maybe it makes you feel a little bit better."For the unversed, the four time NBA champion, Stephen Curry started his business journey in 2013 by signing his endorsement deal with Under Armour.Later, the star player then took control of his entrepreneurial ventures in 2018 by founding his primary corporate umbrella, Thirty Ink, alongside his production company, Unanimous Media.Stephen Curry also launched the Underrated Basketball tour in 2019, followed by the official launch of the standalone Curry Brand within Under Armour in 2020.Four years ago, the NBA icon extended his sports network with Underrated Golf in 2022 and entered the premium spirits industry by launching Gentleman's Cut Bourbon in 2023.Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, stay focused on giving back to children in Oakland as they raise millions for itWhile Stephen Curry has been a pretty successful entrepreneur in the last decade, he and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have also focused on giving back to their hometown.For close to a decade, Stephen Curry and his wife, Ayesha Curry, have raised a whopping $100 million for their foundation, Eat, Learn & Play, as they continue to help more and more children in Oakland.For now, all eyes remain on him as he gears up for the new season.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: LeBron James’ I PROMISE School marks major milestone in Akron as charity celebrates teachers ahead of NBA star’s final season
articles.summary: LeBron James, the four time NBA champion, is gearing up for his last season in the league after playing for two decades.
articles.body: LeBron James, the four time NBA champion, is gearing up for his last season in the league after playing for two decades. While LeBron James has remained committed to his career, the star player has also remained passionate about giving back to Akron. Days ahead of the new season, LeBron James’ foundation’s education wing has now marked a major milestone.LeBron James’ I PROMISE School makes an update about their community ahead of the new seasonA few hours ago, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon star player’s foundation’s education wing, the I PROMISE School, has shared an update.LeBron James’ I PROMISE School posted, “Happy World Teachers’ Day! Today, we celebrate the teachers who show up, believe big and remind our students that there is no limit to what they can become. You see their potential, celebrate every milestone and continue to pour into them day after day. At IPS, we know it takes a village.”The post added, “Our teachers are an important part of that village helping our students grow, dream bigger and break barriers along the way. To our IPS teachers, thank you for believing in our kids & loving them like family. We are so grateful for you. 🍎💚”The I PROMISE School’s social media update about the institution’s teachers has now made many emotional.Set up in 2016, LeBron James’ I PROMISE School has focused on educating thousands of children across Akron.I PROMISE School has also helped in providing access to children coming from underprivileged families in Akron.LeBron James opens up how the I PROMISE School has continued to serve students and be there for them in AkronIn an interview with PEOPLE, the four time NBA champion, LeBron James had opened up about I PROMISE School’s impact in Akron as he said, “A lot of what we do at I Promise School is based on our experience and that’s what makes the connection so real.”The Philadelphia 76ers’ star player added, “We have a mutual understanding of each other and what we’re going through, and I think that gives us all the drive we need to succeed for one another.”LeBron James further reflected on how his foundation has tried to help more and more children in Akron as he said, “We’re also delivering meals to homes, making sure our kids have the tools they need for online learning, just anything we can do to help during this time, which we know is particularly challenging for the families in our program,” he explains.For now, all eyes remain on LeBron James as he gears up for his final season on the court with the Philadelphia 76ers, as many remain excited about his performance.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luka Doncic injury update: Latest on Lakers leader following scary preseason limping moment
articles.summary: Lakers fans held their breath at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento on Monday night.
articles.body: Lakers fans held their breath at Golden 1 Center in Sacramento on Monday night. Luka Doncic was seen limping at one point during the preseason opener against the Kings, and the worry spread fast on a roster built around one player. Doncic had not played an official game since April 2. The 27-year-old guard still logged 16 minutes in a 127-103 win and spoke afterward about how his body felt. Coach JJ Redick also weighed in on what Doncic did differently this summer, and the two accounts do not match perfectly.Is Luka Doncic hurt after limping in the Lakers' preseason opener?The post-game coverage does not point to a serious injury. Also, it is unclear what caused the limp, but Doncic still finished with 21 points on 5-of-12 shooting, plus two rebounds, three assists, and two steals. Afterward, Doncic reported feeling great and called the team impressive."I'm really happy to be back," Doncic said after five or six months away. Rest played a role, too. Doncic sat out the playoffs and skipped national team duty, so the season starts with solid health and a fresh mind.Doncic credited wings Matisse Thybulle and Ziaire Williams for the defensive start, and the Lakers forced 27 turnovers, something they had not done since 2000. Rookie Cameron Carr scored 19, Quentin Grimes had 16 and Williams added 13, and the last two made a case for starting spots. Doncic also said the Lakers have plenty of room to improve, especially in the move from defense to offense.What did JJ Redick say about Doncic's shape this season?Lakers coach JJ Redick said Doncic worked hard all summer and arrived at camp in "fantastic shape." According to Redick, Doncic played less live basketball than in past summers and spent that time on cardio and running instead. For years, Doncic was known for playing himself into shape during the season, so a camp arrival in good condition stands out.Doncic described it more simply. "I didn't change much," Doncic said, pointing to extra rest and the break from national team play. Both versions can be true. Less time on court and more running would fit neatly with a summer of extra rest.Last season, Doncic played 64 games, one short of the threshold for season awards, while averaging 33.5 points, 7.7 rebounds and 8.3 assists. With LeBron James gone, the Lakers now build around Doncic, and Redick has made conditioning a theme for the whole roster.The Lakers host the Kings on Thursday, then face the Warriors on Oct. 13 and the Nuggets on Oct. 16. articles.title: Aces' Jewell Loyd downgraded to out for Wednesday's playoff game vs. Valkyries
articles.summary: Loyd suffered a lower-body injury during Sunday's Game 1 loss.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces guard Jewell Loyd has been downgraded to out for Wednesday's playoff game against the Golden State Valkyries. She had been listed as doubtful.

Loyd is dealing with a left leg injury sustained in the third quarter of the Game 1 loss on Sunday. She couldn't return to the game.

Head coach Becky Hammon spoke to the media Tuesday and said they didn't yet have a report on Loyd. "We're trying to ramp them up, but now we've got to see how they feel and recover off of this little workout." A few hours later, the guard was listed as doubtful due to the injury.

On Wednesday, Hammon said Loyd was "likely" to be out for the contest. Hours later, the guard was downgraded to out.

Loyd isn't one of Las Vegas' star players, but if she is sidelined for the game, it will still hurt the Aces. The guard averages 8 points, 2.3 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game.

Loyd averaged 25.9 minutes per game, though, and Las Vegas is already short on backcourt depth.

Before the injury Sunday, Loyd hadn't made either of her two shots from beyond the arc. She did play 17 minutes and added two rebounds and an assist.

Aces guard Dana Evans was listed as questionable and has been upgraded to probable. Forward Steph Talbot is considered questionable. Evans is dealing with a right knee issue, while Talbot is dealing with a lower left leg injury similar to Loyd's. Hammon said Wednesday both players will be game-time decisions.

With Loyd sidelined on Sunday night, guard Mai Yamamoto saw more playing time. She played 19 minutes, above her 15.1 average. Yamamoto finished the loss with just two points and an assist.

Las Vegas is down 1-0 in the best-of-five series.

articles.title: Trail Blazers have 'set themselves up to fail' by firing Braiden Bell over teenage tweets, attorney says
articles.summary: Braiden Bell's attorney calls the Portland Trail Blazers' morals clause "immoral" for firing the announcer over social media posts he made at age 15.
articles.body: Firing a grown man over social media posts he wrote as a 15-year-old kid has put the Portland Trail Blazers in hot water. Newly hired play-by-play announcer Braiden Bell was ousted shortly after taking the job when a local news report surfaced crude posts from 2012 and 2013. While Bell has navigated the situation with grace and issued an immediate public apology for his teenage posts, getting back into the Blazers' good graces remains a steep battle. Now, Bell's attorney, Arnie Herz, is pushing back against the franchise's approach. Speaking with OutKick, Herz addressed the societal shift toward retroactively punishing individuals for online posts. MEDIA SINKS TO NEW LOW BY DIGGING UP TWEETS THAT GOT ANNOUNCER FIRED BY COWARDLY BLAZERS "What we've become as a society is very much a gotcha and a teardown mindset," Herz explained. "If everything came to light of your most insensitive comments, your worst behaviors, you wouldn't be able to sustain this zero tolerance." Herz added that if the organization strictly enforced such a policy across the board, "I don't think there would be a single player, single member in the front office, a single coach, or a single fan who would be able to participate." Herz pointed out the utter absurdity of holding anyone to such a standard. "The only possible person who could be the play-by-play announcer based on a zero-tolerance standard is Mother Teresa," Herz added. "But there's three problems with that. One, she's not alive. Two, she knew nothing about basketball. And three, I don't think she'd want the job. So, that's it. There's no Saints, except in New Orleans, in football, and obviously, that's just the name." THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! While morals clauses are common in sports, Herz argued applying them to teenage posts stretches the rule past common sense. "I'm a big fan of a morals clause," Herz noted. "I totally understand a team that has someone on their personnel who does something egregious, like being charged with a felony, making horrific comments as a grown-up in the course of their employment. ... But having a morals clause that's so broad that it is going to ensnare comments made by a teenage boy in early teenage years, 15, is immoral." "A morals clause properly drafted serves a very valuable moral purpose," Herz added. "And a morals clause overly broad becomes itself immoral. I think that's what we have here." Herz argued Portland's unyielding stance clashes directly with its own past. "Not only do they have no precedence, there's very few organizations in the world of sports that have shown greater leniency to giving second, third, fourth, and fifth chances than the Blazer organization," Herz stated. "This is an organization that's had significant issues in the past and have members on their staff on the court and off the court who have done far, far, far worse than what Mr. Bell did." He added that on-court value changes the rules entirely. NEW YORK TIMES LOSES DEFAMATION SUIT, ORDERED TO PAY $9.25M TO FORMER ALABAMA BASKETBALL PLAYER "When you're a big star, you make a lot of money, the team very much depends on you, the league depends on you, you get more slack," Herz admitted. "That's just the reality. If Braiden could hit a three and defend players like the starting five, we wouldn't be here right now." Herz warned that the franchise's stance sets a troublesome precedent for future hires. "If I'm legal counsel for the Blazers, I'm saying to the Blazers: 'You have to reinstate this guy. If you're gonna fire him for this, every single person on social media is gonna be scrutinizing every hire you make, every player you have on your roster, and it's going to consume you,'" Herz advised. "You've set yourself up to fail. Back off." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Herz urged both sides to acknowledge their mistakes and resolve the matter constructively. "Just like Braiden made a mistake, the Blazers made a mistake," Herz concluded. "Take responsibility, take accountability, let's move forward. Our goal is really to use this as a learning experience for everyone so that everyone could win." Send us your thoughts: alejandro.avila@outkick.com / Follow along on X: @alejandroaveela

articles.title: Dana Altman ends nearly four decade coaching career at Oregon: 'Stepping away is truly painful'
articles.summary: Dana Altman retires as Oregon Ducks basketball head coach after 16 seasons, with assistant Tony Stubblefield named interim for the upcoming campaign.
articles.body: The coach who has manned the sideline for more Oregon men’s basketball games than any other coach is going off into the sunset. Dana Altman has decided to retire after 16 seasons with the Ducks and nearly four decades as a Division I coach, the school announced Wednesday. Altman, 68, first took over Oregon’s program in 2010. Assistant coach Tony Stubblefield will assume Altman’s responsibilities on an interim basis beginning next season. "I've loved every minute of coaching here, and stepping away is difficult and truly painful," Altman said in a statement. "I love coaching, it's what I know best and what I've been fortunate enough to do for almost five decades. "... It's been the honor of my life to coach the Ducks," he added. Oregon football coach Dan Lanning was among those offering praise for Altman. "A great mentor, sees the game, and obviously a Hall of Fame coach with what he’s been able to accomplish," Lanning said. "I love his story, and how grounded he is, and he’s as good as they come." BASKETBALL HALL OF FAMER DON NELSON DEAD AT 86 Altman’s announcement came as a surprise, but the Ducks have experienced some upheaval. They struggled last season, going 12-20, and the program lost nine players to the transfer portal and three to graduation in the offseason. articles.title: Fans are wondering if Florida Panthers are cursed as another star exits game Wednesday night
articles.summary: Aleksander Barkov's latest injury and Brad Marchand's scary exit have Florida Panthers fans wondering if the team is cursed after back-to-back Cups.
articles.body: A little less than 16 months ago, the question surrounding the National Hockey League was whether or not the Florida Panthers were on the fast track to becoming the sport's next dynasty. They had just vanquished the Edmonton Oilers for the second year in a row to capture back-to-back Stanley Cups, and many fans were wondering if they had a chance to become the first team to three-peat since the New York Islanders won four straight from 1980-83. Then the injuries started to pile up, beginning right as the Cup celebration ended with star winger Matthew Tkachuk needing adductor surgery. OTTAWA SENATORS OWNER CLAIMS KEITH TKACHUK AND MATTHEW TKACHUK SWAYED BRADY'S TRADE REQUEST Tkachuk would be out for the first half of the season, but his injury was only the tip of the iceberg. The Panthers famously lost captain Aleksander Barkov for the year thanks to a torn ACL, and other key contributors like sniper Sam Reinhart, defender Seth Jones, and two-way wizard Anton Lundell also missed multiple weeks in the season with a bevy of injuries. 2026 was supposed to be the bounceback year for the Cats, as Barkov and the rest of his merry band of champions were thought to be fully healthy. Then, just two games into the season, the Panthers captain went down awkwardly in an eerily similar fashion to his ACL injury a little more than a year earlier, causing Florida fans to wince. Barkov was given a supremely positive diagnosis relative to what the news could have been — a 6-8 week recovery period — but before Panthers fans could even finish their sighs of relief, another integral piece to their 2025 Cup run went down in a heap. When it rains it pours, and Florida losing Brad Marchand for any stretch of time is less than ideal. The 38-year-old forward defied Father Time during the 2025 Stanley Cup Playoffs, scoring 10 goals and 10 assists in 23 postseason games, but this latest injury could be one that keeps him out for a while. Marchand was already recovering from an injury at the end of last season, and the fears are this could be serious given the fact he was unable to put any weight on his leg as he was helped off the ice Wednesday night (the most likely outcome seems to be an MCL injury). THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! This rash of injuries over the past year plus has fans wondering whether the Panthers sold their souls for those back-to-back Cups. Fellow OutKick writer and hockey fanatic Matt Reigle even asked me if there were any electrical substations located near Amarant Bank Arena. While I'm not sure about that, I have opined for quite some time now that the Cats may be cursed, and the Marchy injury isn't exactly helping to assuage those concerns. If you're a Panthers fan looking for a positive, then consider the fact that the Barkov injury wasn't as bad as initially feared, and there is a world where Marchand gets a similar diagnosis. The Cats also went out and acquired Ottawa Senators captain Brady Tkachuk to help bolster the depth on the roster as well, so if anyone can withstand the injury bug early in the season, it's Florida. Also, we are only four games into the year, but the Panthers are leading the division even without their captain and their playoff ace. articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton buys student section tickets for Iowa State students in his preseason return
articles.summary: In his return to his alma mater, Tyrese Haliburton bought out the student section tickets for all Iowa State students for the Pacers first preseason game in...
articles.body:
AMES, Iowa — Iowa State students got in free to Tyrese Haliburton's homecoming game Wednesday night, thanks to the superstar himself.

Sixteen months after tearing his Achilles in the 2025 NBA Finals, Haliburton is making his return to NBA action at Hilton Coliseum, his alma mater, for Indiana's first preseason game against the Minnesota Timberwolves .

In his return, he wanted to cultivate the college basketball fan environment. So, he paid for every single student section ticket himself.

"I know that nobody is as passionate about Iowa State as the current students, so I'm excited for them to be there and just experience all that," Haliburton said at practice on Wednesday. "The college basketball environment is much better than the NBA, from a top to bottom perspective, so I'm excited for there to be a college basketball vibe in there."

Pacers' Tyrese Haliburton visits Peyton Manning Children's Hospital

The student section at Hilton Coliseum sits behind both baskets, and the line to get a spot wrapped around the building by the time doors opened an hour and half before game time. Inside, every student got a yellow 'Cyclone Hali' t-shirt, which depicted Haliburton wrapped up in a cyclone.

Haliburton didn't know how many tickets he bought, Pacers head coach Carlisle said, but he estimated it was in the thousands.

"This is just another one of those amazing gestures of Tyrese's family," Carlisle said. "We pulled in here, and it took a while to get in here, there's a huge line at the front door, and it looks like a bunch of students. I've been in here for games a couple times, and this is one of the best venue in all of college basketball, and so I'm expecting it's going to be pretty cool here tonight."

Haliburton knows, too, that not all the students will be rooting for him — especially because the majority of Iowans in this area are Timberwolves fans. There were some students in Timberwolves jerseys in line, and even someone in a Milwaukee Bucks jersey waiting to get in.

The student section at Hilton Coliseum spans behind both baskets, and the line was wrapped around the building by the time students were let in.

"I don't know if it'll be all Pacers fans in there, it'll be some Timberwolves fans too," Haliburton said on Wednesday with a laugh. "But it'll be fun, I'm excited for everybody to experience Hilton Coliseum."

articles.title: Atlanta Dream to call State Farm Arena home in 2027 amid WNBA boom
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream will have a new home with 17,000 seats in 2027. State Farm Arena is now the WNBA team's base.
articles.body:
ATLANTA ― The Atlanta Dream are getting new digs for the 2027 WNBA season.

On Tuesday, the organization announced it will call State Farm Arena home next year. The move comes as part of a multi-year agreement with the facility to host home games and amid record growth for the league. Next season, the WNBA will move to 50 games and State Farm will host the Dream's 25 home contests.

The Dream sold out every game during the last three seasons at its current home, Gateway Center Arena, a space which holds 3,500-plus seats. Within that same span, Atlanta played multiple games at State Farm, including six regular-season and two playoff games this season, with another postseason game tipping off Wednesday against the New York Liberty . The venue was sold out eight times and had multiple games at full capacity, with more than 17,000 seats.

"We didn't have playoff games (at State Farm Arena) last year ... but we had a couple of games there, and they felt like playoff games. So I think for us to have had those during the season and have the outcome that we had, I think it helps us get ready for this environment," Dream guard Rhyne Howard said.

"Our fans are gonna show up every day, whether we're here (at Gateway Center Area or) whether we're in State Farm, but I think being able to have all of our games there ― it gives us more. Obviously, there's more people, but I think you give more people the opportunity to come cheer for you."

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

"Something (Dream co-owner) Suzanne Abair said to me ... she said, we don't believe in betting on women because when you place a bet, you expect that you might lose your money. But when you invest, you expect a return," Morgan Shaw Parker, the team president and chief operating officer, said on Wednesday. "You have to invest it. It takes a lot out of our leadership, takes a lot out of our ownership. It costs. The operating budget is extremely important, but how do you maintain that? You set the vision, and you don't take your foot off the gas."

Shaw Parker also said the addition of Angel Reese impacted the decision to move arenas.

"It was a huge impact to our organization with Angel coming. What I've always said is we would have never been able to attract someone like Angel Reese if we weren't ready to receive her," Shaw Parker said. "Atlanta is here for her. She is here for Atlanta, but what she's brought is undeniable."

Atlanta, which joined the league as an expansion franchise in 2008, began its WNBA tenure at Philips Arena (now renamed State Farm Arena) the same year and played at the venue through the 2016 season. It then spent two seasons at Georgia Tech's McCamish Pavilion from 2017-2018 before returning to State Farm in 2019. Following the 2019 season, the Dream moved to Gateway Center in 2020, where it has played seven seasons.

Shaw Parker confirmed the Dream are also exploring plans for a women's specific arena in Atlanta in the future.

Atlanta is currently competing in the 2026 WNBA playoffs as the No. 4 seed after finishing 30-14 for the second consecutive season. It swept the Washington Mystics, 2-0, in the first round and is currently in the semifinals for the first time since 2018. The Dream are up 1-0 over the Liberty as of this publication.

articles.title: Buss siblings file formal opposition after Jeanie Buss' attempts to block remaining sale of Lakers stake
articles.summary: The Buss family legal battle over their remaining stake in the Lakers appears to be far from over.
articles.body:
The Buss family legal battle over the Los Angeles Lakers continued on Wednesday.

The five Buss siblings who voted to sell the rest of the family trust's shares in the franchise — Jim, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jessie — filed a formal opposition in court on Wednesday after unresolved settlement discussions with their other sister, Jeanie Buss, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.

Jeanie had previously filed a petition in Los Angeles Superior Court to attempt to block the five siblings from selling the family's remaining 17.8% stake in the Lakers, which she claimed was a scheme to remove her from her role as the team's governor.

"Jimmy, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss, the five of six siblings who voted to sell the Trust's shares in the Lakers, today filed their formal opposition, demonstrating that Jeanie Buss's petition is legally and factually baseless," the five siblings said in a statement. "While discussions among the siblings continue, their focus remains on facilitating the proposed transaction and the Trust's participation in it, while ensuring that all beneficiaries, including Jeanie, are treated equally. "Today's filing is a necessary step to protect those interests and ensure the transaction proceeds on schedule."

"Jimmy, Johnny, Janie, Joey and Jesse Buss, the five of six siblings who voted to sell the Trust's shares in the Lakers, today filed their formal opposition, demonstrating that Jeanie Buss's petition is legally and factually baseless," the five siblings said in a statement. "While discussions among the siblings continue, their focus remains on facilitating the proposed transaction and the Trust's participation in it, while ensuring that all beneficiaries, including Jeanie, are treated equally.

"Today's filing is a necessary step to protect those interests and ensure the transaction proceeds on schedule."

Mark Walter, who purchased a majority of the Buss family's share of the Lakers last year, announced earlier this fall that he was selling his stake in the team to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger at a record $12.5 billion valuation. The five siblings then reportedly voted to invoke a "tag-along" clause to sell their remaining stake in the team to Kushner and Iger.

Jeanie, however, does not want to sell and called any vote to sell the team "void." She filed a 97-page petition that included five causes of action , and argued that selling the team doesn't make any financial sense. She also asked the court to instruct her co-trustees to observe a 2017 court order that requires they "take all actions reasonably available to ensure Jeanie's appointment as Controlling Owner" of the Lakers.

NBA rules require that a team governor own at least 15% of a team. Jeanie was going to remain in her role as governor for the next four years under Kushner and Iger, though that can't happen if her siblings prevail and they sell the rest of their shares.

This is just the latest feud among the Buss siblings since their father, Jerry Buss, died in 2013. The biggest issue was back in 2017, when Jeanie fired Jim as the Lakers' head of basketball operations, which led to Johnny challenging her control of the team. Jerry left her control of the team as part of the trust, and she ended up winning a court decision that said her siblings were obligated to ensure she remains the team's controlling owner.

It's unclear if that order still applies, as the Buss family is not the controlling owner of the team anymore. Jeanie simply wants to keep control of the team's minority ownership of the team.

The move to sell the team by the siblings makes sense, especially since Jerry put a "last man standing" provision in his trust. That would transfer ownership of the team and funds to the remaining siblings when one of the six of them dies, rather than to their own families. But if the siblings sell before their own deaths, they can pass money along to their respective families and children.

Clearly, things within the Buss family haven't settled down any. With a formal opposition now filed, the family is headed toward another, likely messy, court battle.

articles.title: Jusuf Nurkic Out 4+ Weeks with Injury, Latest Updates on Jazz Star Ahead of NBA Season
articles.summary: Utah Jazz center Jusuf Nurkić suffered a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe in his right foot and will miss at least four weeks, per NBA on Prime senior insider Chris Haynes.
articles.body:
Utah Jazz center Jusuf Nurkić suffered a partial plantar plate tear of the second toe in his right foot and will miss at least four weeks, per NBA on Prime senior insider Chris Haynes .

The 32-year-old Nurkić is entering his 13th NBA season and second with the Jazz. The 6'11", 290-pound big man averaged 10.9 points on 50.3 percent shooting, 10.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists in 26.4 minutes per game over 41 contests (36 starts) last season.

Nurkić was slated to start the season as Utah's center again, and that was his spot Sunday, when Utah began the preseason at the Denver Nuggets. He played 11 minutes and posted four points, five rebounds and four assists in a 109-97 victory.

Nurkić did not participate in an open practice on Monday, per Shreyas Laddha of the Salt Lake Tribune .

He did not play on Tuesday in Utah's 117-106 preseason home loss to Denver.

Jaxson Hayes, an eight-year veteran who played for the New Orleans Pelicans and Los Angeles Lakers before signing a two-year deal with Utah this summer, started for Nurkić.

Utah also has Kyle Filipowski and Mo Bamba on the roster to play center.

Looking ahead, a four-week timeline means Nurkić will miss Utah's first eight regular-season games (Oct. 21-Nov. 4) at minimum.

As Ben Anderson of KSL Sports noted, the Jazz can bring someone else aboard.

Nurkić fared well for Utah last year for a Jazz team that needed center help after Walker Kessler missed nearly all of 2025-26 with a labral tear in his left shoulder. He proved to be a big asset down low, especially on the boards.

Unfortunately, Nurkic missed 41 games, including the final 27 contests after undergoing nose surgery for a deviated septum. Now this season has started with more bad luck on the health front.

Hopefully Nurkić gets back to 100 percent health ASAP and returns soon after this four-week timeline, as Utah clearly relied on him to make a strong impact this season.

articles.title: Will Wade Jokes Lane Kiffin is LSU's 'Most Controversial Coach' Amid Roster Criticism
articles.summary: LSU's decision to bring back Will Wade as the head coach of its men's basketball program was certainly a controversial one considering he was previously fired following allegations he violated NCAA rules.
articles.body:
LSU's decision to bring back Will Wade as the head coach of its men's basketball program was certainly a controversial one considering he was previously fired following allegations he violated NCAA rules.

But there's another head coach on campus who is stealing some of the headlines when it comes to controversy.

"A lot (has) changed since the first time I was here," Wade told the Rotary Club of Baton Rouge, per Christopher Kamrani of The Athletic. "There's two massive changes: the first big change is I'm no longer the most controversial coach on campus. I've been happy to kind of pass that along. The second part is, we were just a little bit ahead of our time with NIL."

It was, of course, a joking reference to football head coach Lane Kiffin.

Kiffin's departure from Ole Miss to take the LSU job ahead of last season's College Football Playoff was a notable one. He did not remain with the Rebels for their CFP run and brought some of the team's assistant coaches with him.

There was also the prolonged controversy early this season when Kiffin and LSU tried to bring back tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris even after they previously signed with NFL rosters.

They ultimately never played for the Tigers, but it generated plenty of headlines.

Wade's program is also facing some controversy and question marks of its own that goes beyond the head-turning decision to bring him back as the head coach.

As Kamrani explained, many of the team's scholarship players are awaiting updates regarding their eligibility. There are just four players listed on the official roster , as of Wednesday.

"I believe that on Nov. 3, we will roll out there with every player eligible that is within those guidelines, that's within the SEC guidelines," Wade said. "And I believe all the international kids, all the fifth-year kids, will be eligible."

LSU opens its regular season on Nov. 3 against LSU New Orleans.

articles.title: Tyrese Haliburton returns from Achilles injury in preseason game in Ames, where he bought out the Iowa State student section
articles.summary: Tyrese Haliburton missed all of last season while recovering from an Achilles injury he suffered in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals.
articles.body:
Tyrese Haliburton made his return at a familiar place on Wednesday night.

Haliburton took the court in the Indiana Pacers' 123-112 win over the Minnesota Timberwolves to open their preseason slate on Wednesday night at Hilton Coliseum in Ames, Iowa. Haliburton spent two years playing for the Cyclones at Hilton Coliseum before he was selected with the No. 12 overall pick in 2020.

The contest marked Haliburton's first in more than 16 months. He tore his right Achilles during Game 7 of the NBA Finals in 2025. The Oklahoma City Thunder eventually won that game, which stopped the Pacers from claiming what would have been their first NBA championship. Haliburton averaged 18.6 points and 9.2 assists per game that season.

The injury then knocked Haliburton out for the entire 2025-26 campaign. The Pacers finished with just a 19-63 record without him, which marked their worst outing in franchise history.

But after a year out of action, Haliburton entered training camp confident he'd have no restrictions and be ready to pick up right where he left off.

"I've worked really hard to get to where I am right now," Haliburton said late last month . "I'm a big believer in my work. I've put in an unbelievable amount of time to get to where I am today, so all my belief comes from that."

Haliburton finished with seven points and six assists in the 16 minutes that he played. He got his first bucket almost instantly, hitting an easy jumper from the elbow in the opening minutes.

Haliburton took an extra step to embrace his homecoming before Wednesday night. He actually purchased tickets for the entire student section at Hilton Coliseum, and the university held a lottery for students to attend the game for free. Fans got special Haliburton shirts, and Haliburton addressed the crowd before the game.

Haliburton played for the Cyclones from 2018-2020. He averaged 15.2 points and 6.5 assists per game during his second season while earning All-Big 12 honors.

"I think it'll be fun for everybody," Haliburton said Tuesday before the game, via ESPN . "I know there's nobody as passionate about Iowa State as the current students."

The Pacers will open the regular season against the New Orleans Pelicans on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Stewart's Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Beat Liberty in WNBA Playoffs Game 2
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream are one win away from their first trip to the WNBA Finals in 13 years.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream are one win away from their first trip to the WNBA Finals in 13 years.

Atlanta outlasted the New York Liberty 101-98 in an overtime thriller in Game 2 of their semifinals series in the 2026 WNBA playoffs on Wednesday at State Farm Arena. Even with Allisha Gray (finger) sidelined, they seized a 2-0 series lead thanks to a late basket from Naz Hillmon and massive free throws from Angel Reese.

New York had a chance to tie it, but Breanna Stewart's desperation heave after the visitors did not call timeout fell short after Sabrina Ionescu committed a critical turnover the previous possession.

It seemed as if Marine Fauthoux was going to be the hero when she drained a dramatic three to force overtime, but it was the Dream who controlled the extra period.

All five Atlanta starters scored in double figures with Reese and Jordin Canada leading the way, which was enough to outlast an excellent game from Stewart.

Nobody in the entire WNBA has been playing better basketball of late than the Dream, who won nine of their final 10 regular-season games and then captured each of their first three postseason contests by double digits.

One of those was a 10-point win over the Liberty in Game 1, although Wednesday figured to be more of a challenge on paper with Gray sidelined.

Dealing with Stewart also made it more of a challenge.

The two-time MVP was quiet by her standards with 19 points in Game 1 but came out on fire in Game 2. She poured in 25 points in the first half alone by hitting from the outside, attacking the lane and getting to the free-throw line.

Stewart was unstoppable, while Jonquel Jones provided important secondary scoring when Atlanta was too focused on the eight-time All-Star. Yet the Dream still took a two-point lead into intermission thanks in large part to a barrage of three-point shooting.

Canada and Rhyne Howard led the way from the perimeter, but even Reese hit from beyond the arc. Reese also converted multiple and-1 opportunities and showed off why she is the Defensive Player of the Year with a blocked shot and steal while dealing with New York's star-studded frontcourt.

The theme of Stewart and Jones against Atlanta's three-point shooting continued after halftime with Isobel Borlase providing a shooting spark off the bench to create some temporary breathing room for the home team.

However, New York closed the quarter on a 7-0 run to cut the deficit to one heading to the fourth with Stewart assisting Fauthoux on back-to-back baskets to swing momentum in the visitors' favor.

While both offenses played freely for most of the game, it was a different story early in the fourth when they completely bogged down. Much of that was because of suffocating defense on both sides, including when Reese swatted Ionescu in a play that brought the crowd to its feet.

With defense like that, all it took was a timely basket or two to create some separation. And the Dream got just that when Reese scored in the paint and Howard converted an and-1 to open up a six-point advantage in the final two minutes.

Yet it wasn't enough to win in regulation.

Ionescu hit an important three, but it was the triple from Fauthoux with 10 seconds remaining that stood out the most. She caught Stewart's pass in rhythm and buried the open look, while Howard's potential game-winner rimmed out on the ensuing possession.

Despite the stunning finish to the fourth quarter, the Dream bounced back in overtime with timely plays on both ends of the floor and are now in full control of the series.

Jordin Canada was also a key contributor for Atlanta, finishing with 23 points, eight assists, five rebounds and one steal. Canada shot 9-of-15 on field goals, which included 3-of-6 from behind the arc.

The Liberty couldn't pick up their first win of the series despite an impressive performance from Breanna Stewart, as she scored a game-high 35 points on 11-of-21 shooting.

In the second game of the day, Golden State was in control for the majority of the contest.

The Valkyries took a double-digit lead in the first quarter and maintained a 64-47 edge with just under two minutes remaining in the third.

Las Vegas immediately went on a 27-10 run to tie the contest with two minutes left in the fourth, though.

The Aces briefly jumped in front with a layup by A'ja Wilson, but Golden State gained the lead once again with a three-pointer from Veronica Burton.

Las Vegas couldn't respond, as the Valkyries hit free throws to seal the win.

Tiffany Hayes scored a team-high 21 points in 17 minutes off the bench for Golden State, while Gabby Williams chipped in with 20 points and five rebounds to go along with three assists.

The final score took a backseat to the debut of the No. 4 overall pick of the 2026 NBA draft, though, and the North Carolina product scored in double figures.

Here is a look at how his numbers stacked up in the contest.

Chicago hasn't advanced past the play-in tournament since the 2021-22 campaign and hasn't won a playoff series since the 2014-15 season. There hasn't been much to be excited about for the franchise for years, but that could change in 2026-27.

After all, Wilson is a high-flying foundational cornerpiece who could thrive for years to come. Even if the Bulls struggle from a record perspective this season, his potential on a team with young talent elsewhere with Matas Buzelis and Josh Giddey could provide reason for optimism.

And Wednesday was the first chance for fans to see him in person, even if it was just the preseason.

It wasn't all good, as Wilson struggled from the outside while missing all four of his three-point attempts. If he is going to fully live up to expectations, he will need to find a way to hit some shots from beyond the arc when defenders collapse on Buzelis and Giddey.

But he did more than enough to make up for the perimeter shooting woes.

Wilson's first basket was a fadeaway jumper, and he also mixed in a turnaround jumper and impressive reverse finish at the rim when attacking the basket. Finding different ways to score will be important, especially when he sees different defensive looks throughout his rookie campaign.

The rookie also gave the fans what they wanted when he broke free in transition and threw down a two-handed dunk. The high-flyer figures to play above the rim whenever possible, and he wasted little time putting on a show in his first game.

There is still plenty to work on, as the Bulls will surely want him to be more of a factor on the glass. Efficiency was also a concern at 6-of-15 from the field, although that will likely come with more experience.

Ultimately, there was plenty to be excited about for Wilson in his first game action.

articles.title: ‘Future MVP,’ ‘Finals Appearance Before Caitlin Clark’ — Angel Reese Draws Major Praise As Clutch Performance Moves Dream 1 Win From WNBA Finals
articles.summary: Angel Reese has given the Atlanta Dream plenty of reasons to believe this could be their year. The recently named WNBA Defensive Player of the Year has carri...
articles.body:
Angel Reese has given the Atlanta Dream plenty of reasons to believe this could be their year. The recently named WNBA Defensive Player of the Year has carried her regular-season form into the playoffs, helping Atlanta build momentum at just the right time.

Reese came through again on Wednesday in a tight battle against the New York Liberty. WNBA fans had plenty to say about her performance, particularly how she handled the pressure late in the game.

Angel Reese Earns WNBA Fans' Praise After Delivering in Overtime Against Liberty

Atlanta pulled off a 101-98 overtime win against the New York Liberty in Game 2 of the WNBA semifinals, with Reese putting up 23 points and 7 rebounds. She also had 2 assists, 2 blocks, and a steal, going 8-for-16 and hitting 1 of 2 attempts from beyond the arc. The Dream now lead 2-0 and need just one more win to reach the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

The three-time All-Star scored six of Atlanta's 13 overtime points and knocked down two clutch free throws with 4.3 seconds remaining to help seal the victory. Naz Hillmon had put the Dream ahead with a layup at the 20.8-second mark before Reese helped finish the job. Atlanta now heads to New York for Game 3 on Friday with a chance to secure its place in the championship series.

Reese's showing against New York drew plenty of reactions from WNBA fans, with some already making bold predictions about her future in the league.

"She's about to sweep the Liberty, but she isn't good right? Future MVP candidate," a YouTuber wrote .

"Reese finals appearance before Caitlin Clark," a sports fan added .

Reese's postseason success has also fueled comparisons with other prominent basketball stars. Some fans have focused on how quickly she has found herself competing for a championship appearance, while others have pointed to her improvement from one playoff game to the next.

"Angel Reese has increased her scoring in every playoff game of her career so far," Real App posted .

"Angel Reese ring before Luka [Dončić]," one fan remarked .

The comparisons continued beyond the WNBA, with another fan bringing Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid into the conversation.

"Angel gonna make a finals before Embiid conference finals," a WNBA supporter predicted .

Still, there was also recognition of what Reese actually did on the court, particularly when the game tightened in overtime.

"Angel Reese, man. Her poise and IQ in that overtime was absolutely insane," another tweeted .

StatMuse joined the conversation with a comparison of Reese's and Clark's postseason success.

"Career win percentage in the playoffs: 100% – Angel Reese 20% – Caitlin Clark."

Reese's growing playoff reputation is backed by her production. She has scored more points in each of her four postseason appearances, going from 13 in her playoff debut to 15, 17, and now 23. More importantly for Atlanta, she has kept the Dream unbeaten.

The comparisons and individual predictions can wait. Atlanta still needs another win, and New York has a chance to respond on its home floor. Reese, though, has already shown she can handle a high-pressure playoff finish. One more victory would put her and the Dream on the WNBA's biggest stage.

articles.title: WNBA playoff winners and losers include Angel Reese's clutch gene, Aces
articles.summary: The Dream and Valkyries are one win each from advancing to the WNBA Finals. Here are the winners and losers from Game 2 of the semifinals.
articles.body:
Game 2 of the semifinals of the 2026 WNBA playoffs is in the books and both home teams held serve.

The No. 4 seed Atlanta Dream are up 2-0 in their best-of-five series with the No. 8 seed New York Liberty . Atlanta won 101-98 in an overtime thriller on Wednesday, Oct. 7, at State Farm Arena.

After trailing by 17 points in the third quarter, the defending champion Aces got their first lead with 90 seconds left. Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton helped the the No. 2 seeded Valkyries hold on for a 83-81 victory and 2-0 series lead at Chase Center in San Francisco.

Here are the winners and losers from Game 2 of each semifinal series.

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Dream forward Angel Reese's clutch free throws

Angel Reese likely nailed the biggest free throws of her WNBA career ― twice. When the Dream needed Reese to step to the line and make clutch shots, she did. Reese sank two free throws with 15 seconds left in regulation to put the Dream up by three, and then again in overtime with four seconds remaining to put the Dream up 101-98. Reese's free throws sealed a 2-0 series lead in the semifinal series. The Dream All-Star showed zero fear with the game on the line, and touched on keeping emotions in check down the stretch.

"We were just talking about managing our emotions and valuing possessions, something that we lived by all year, and I think we did that. Obviously, we got a really good look going into overtime, so we wanted to make sure we stayed poised," Reese said postgame. "(DeWanna Bonner) told us (that) usually the first team that scores is the team that wins that overtime, and she kept telling us that. So she gave us that confidence, and we felt it."

Playoff Stewie is fully activated. New York Liberty forward Breanna Stewart imposed her will early in Game 2 , becoming the first player in WNBA playoff history to record 35 points, 10-plus rebounds and five-plus assists. Stewart finished with 11 boards and six assists.

The Liberty were looking for Stewart early and often on Wednesday. She had 15 points in the first quarter, shooting 5-of-6 from the field and 2-of-2 from the 3-point line. She added another 10 points in the second quarter to improve to 8-of-9 from the field, 2-of-2 from the 3-point line and 7-of-9 from the free-throw line.

Stewart's 25-point first half is tied for the third-highest scoring half in playoff history. Angel McCoughtry holds the record with 27 points scored in a half in 2012, while Stewart recorded 26 points in a half in 2022.

It may be hard to believe, but Tiffany Hayes was done with the WNBA a couple of years ago. Now the Valkyries are a win away from the WNBA Finals with help from the Valkyries guard, who led the charge in the Game 2 win with 21 points off the bench.

Hayes came out of retirement to sign with the Aces ahead of the 2024 season and won Sixth Player of the Year. Las Vegas' quest for three straight WNBA titles was thwarted by the New York Liberty in the semifinals that season.

Hayes opted to sign with the Valkyries in free agency after she said she planned to run it back with the Aces, but it was clearly the right choice.

"I'm here with a group of people who believe in me. I'm here with a group of people who let me be me when I'm on the court. I'm learning a lot from this group from top to bottom," Hayes said during a postgame interview on NBC's broadcast when asked about her confidence. "So definitely no pressure when I'm going in the game. I just know to go out there and give 110% and it always works out in my favor."

Hayes also praised the Valkyries coaching staff, which is led by former Aces assistant Natalie Nakase.

"We got the type of coaches that we can definitely feed off of their energy. And when they give it to us, we give it right back to them. So I think it's easy for us to buy in, especially when we know the direction that we want to go in," Hayes said. "They give it to us straightforward. There's no gray area when they're trying to explain to us what we need to do. So that helps us out a lot."

The Liberty and Dream game was a wild ride. There were six players between both teams playing with at least three fouls and three players who had at least five fouls. By the time the final buzzer sounded, there were a staggering 43 fouls, 29 from the first half. Players from New York and Atlanta were frustrated and as time wound down, the officiating crew was thrust into the spotlight again.

With four seconds remaining in overtime, Dream forward Angel Reese stepped to the line to hit free throws. Breanna Stewart said she asked a nearby official if the Liberty had a reset timeout. She asserts that she was told no. However, postgame, Stewart maintained that New York did have one more timeout.

"I asked Kevin (Fahy), I said, 'Do we have a reset timeout?' And he said, 'I'm going to check at the table.' So then he looked to Fatou (Cissoko-Stephens), and she said, 'No.' So, then he told me no. Of course, who knows what would happen in the game, but we would have hopefully a better shot on goal," Stewart said of the final play, her 32-foot 3-point shot after Reese's free throws.

"This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with a reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating. Yeah, OK, I kind of got a good look at the end, but would just love to have some clarity on that situation."

The official todl the pool report, "(Breanna) Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining."

Teams are responsible for managing keeping track of their timeouts. Officials may confirm the status of timeouts with the scorers' table when necessary, but according to the pool report referee, officials do not track timeouts.

The New York Liberty dug themselves into a 2-0 hole in the WNBA playoff semifinal series against the Dream and now face insurmountable odds — no team down two game has come back to win a best-of-five playoff series.

Self-inflicted wounds were the Liberty's demise. New York conceded 28 points on 17 turnovers, making their second straight game of double-digit turnovers in the WNBA playoff semifinal series.

No turnover loomed larger than Sabrina Ionescu's errant pass with 6.5 seconds remaining in overtime as the Liberty trailed 99-98. Instead of capitalizing on an opportunity to take the lead late, the Liberty gave possession to the Dream, who knocked down clutch free throws to seal the win.

"(Sabrina Ionescu) saw multiple defenders and (Jonquel Jones) was open and passed her just a little bit high, but it's so many plays that led to this," Liberty forward Breanna Stewart said after the loss.

Despite the daunting road ahead of them, the Liberty are not giving up. Liberty head coach Chris DeMarco said, "What's important right now is that we focus on Game 3 and that's got to be it. There's nothing we can do about this game, about this season, anything like that. Obviously what happened happened."

After Wednesday's loss, the Aces are facing odds no WNBA team has ever beaten.

The league adapted a best-of-five playoff series for the Finals in 2005 and expanded to the league semifinals in 2016. In that span, every team that has ever fallen into a 2-0 deficit has lost the series.

The closest any team has come was the Phoenix Mercury in 2018, which lost the first two games of their semifinal series to the Storm in Seattle before stacking two wins in Phoenix to force a Game 5. The Storm won Game 5 back on their home court 94-84.

Even when the Aces' faced the Liberty in the 2024 semifinals and fell down 2-0 in New York, they recorded one victory before the Liberty ended the series at Michelob Ultra in Las Vegas with a 76-62 win in Game 4.

"I can't convince them that this is not a must win, because if we lose, we go home, or we stay home. The goal is to get one quarter at a time, and you got to string it together," Hammon said of what she's telling her team ahead of Game 3 against the Valkyries in Las Vegas on Friday.

"We know we're capable of of stringing three in a row. We believe we're capable of that, so that will be the mindset. No reverse psychology, no nothing. Just go out and get it done."

This is the Aces' eight straight semifinals appearance, but Hammon isn't counting on history to inform the future – including the late run the Aces made before Veronica Burton's dagger 3-pointer all but sealed it for the Valkyries.

"I mean it should help, but all the experience, all the records, all the championships, they don't get to carry over. You have to go do this work every time you step out on the court," she said.

"Our little comeback there at the end doesn't carry over. Their threes that they hit early on don't care. Everybody has to come to work and do the work over again and my group understands that."

articles.title: 3 takeaways from Utah basketball’s exhibition opener at UNLV
articles.summary: The Utes built a first-half lead before holding off the Rebels and were led by a pair of playmaking guards.
articles.body:
A new group of Utah basketball players got its first taste of facing someone else Wednesday night, as the Runnin' Utes opened exhibition play with a 79-69 win over UNLV in Las Vegas.

Here are three takeaways from Utah's victory at the Thomas & Mack Center.

"The exhibition games are great for us because you get to play against somebody else. And I don't think it's changed where we need to get to, but with a whole new team, it's good to play together," Utah coach Alex Jensen said.

It was a good day all around for the Utes' guard lineup.

A few hours before tipoff, a school spokesperson shared that Trey Campbell was granted a temporary restraining order in his legal battle with the NCAA over eligibility and is eligible to compete.

Campbell, who played the past four seasons at Northern Iowa, spent the offseason pursuing a fifth year of eligibility in the wake of the NCAA's new eligibility model that will allow student-athletes five years to compete in up to five seasons.

That included filing a lawsuit against the NCAA last month in Utah's Business and Chancery Court, seeking an additional season of eligibility.

It didn't take long for Campbell to make an impact on the floor for Utah in Las Vegas. He hit a pair of early 3-pointers and knocked down two free throws in the game's first six minutes on his way to scoring 11 first-half points.

Campbell had a solid night overall, scoring a team-high 17 points, hitting 3 of 7 3-pointers and adding three rebounds, three assists and two steals in 26 minutes of play.

While Campbell led Utah's guard line from the starting lineup, TJ Burch came off the bench and sparked the Utes.

Burch was active on both ends, scoring 16 points while adding five rebounds, one assist and four steals. He made 8 of 10 free throws, leading the Utes' 21-of-25 effort from the free-throw line.

Defensive effort comes with gains and things to improve

Since taking over the program last season, Jensen has preached the need to set the pace defensively, and that was apparent against the Rebels.

Utah was active defensively throughout the night, and while they struggled at times to finish out defensive possessions, the Utes forced 18 turnovers and converted those into 18 points.

Burch, the Horizon League Defensive Player of the Year at Wright State a season ago, was excellent at directing his teammates, and former Utah Valley guard Jackson Holcombe, a former WAC all-defense honoree, showcased his toughness defensively.

The Utes were still out of position and overly aggressive at times, as they finished with 23 fouls, which led to UNLV shooting 29 free throws — though the Rebels only hit 15 of those free-throw attempts.

There were 11 Utes who played Wednesday night, with nine of those players earning double-digit minutes.

"(The) best aspect is I think we played hard. I think the effort was good," Jensen said. "Now we just got to add the smarts with it."

The starting five included Campbell, Holcombe, Taison Chatman, Alec Anigbata and Malek Gomma. Each played 20-plus minutes.

Burch also played 22 minutes and was the catalyst in Utah's bench outsourcing UNLV 32-12.

Having that opportunity for so many players to earn valuable minutes produced a couple of notable statistics.

As a team, Utah shot 10 of 32 from 3-point range, though the Utes did the majority of their damage in the first half. Utah made 9 of 21 3-pointers in the first 20 minutes — helping them take a 45-35 lead into halftime — then were 1 of 11 in the second half.

The Utes showed off an impressive amount of ball movement, particularly in the first half, and while that waned some in the final 20 minutes, it was evident that Utah may not be as reliant on one or two hot hands this season — several people up and down the roster could be the leading scorer on a given night.

One area for improvement was rebounding, as Utah was out-rebounded 45-37. UNLV had a 16-11 advantage on the offensive boards, though the Utes were better at turning those into second-chance points with a 15-9 edge.

The Utes also had 10 assists on 13 made field goals in the first half before finishing with 15 assists on 24 buckets.

"We have a better feel for rotations and stuff," Jensen said after the win. "But just going back to rebounding and stuff of that nature (are things to work on)."

articles.body:
Damian Lillard entered year 13 of his decorated NBA career with a preseason game against the Golden State Warriors. During the game, the Portland Trail Blazers star point guard looked like a player ready to turn back the clock in his first game since suffering a ruptured Achilles tendon.

"I went to his crib over the offseason and checked out some of his workouts, and he was really getting at it, and he told me like he's going to be back. He said he feels like he's 29 all over again," Haynes said.

articles.title: Peñarroya: "Yo no vine al Partizan para sustituir a Obradovic sino para hacer mi trabajo"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador catalán charla con MARCA sobre cómo superó la grave crisis que se encontró en Belgrado, el 3-0 que disfruta en la Euroliga y un Real Madrid al que visita este jueves
articles.summary: El entrenador catalán charla con MARCA sobre cómo superó la grave crisis que se encontró en Belgrado, el 3-0 que disfruta en la Euroliga y un Real Madrid al que visita este jueves
articles.body: Lo que parecía imposible, lo ha conseguido Joan Peñarroya (Terrasa, 1969). Después de salir del Barcelona, en diciembre del año pasado se embarcó en una misión con tintes suicidas: sacar al Partizan, histórico del baloncesto europeo, de una de las mayores crisis de su historia. Con la afición enfrentada a parte de la plantilla, malos resultados y, sobre todo, tras la dimisión del mito Zeljko Obradovic. El técnico catalán, cuando parecía tener todo en contra, le dio la vuelta a aquella tortilla. Su equipo acabó bien el curso pasado y el presente lo ha empezado con un 3-0 en la Euroliga que nunca había vivido. Este jueves, visita al Real Madrid. Pregunta. En un partido en casa de esta temporada, cuando pisó la pista, recibió la ovación de los 20.000 espectadores. ¿Qué se siente ante algo así? Respuesta. Es emocionante. Es una cosa que uno ha vivido muy pocas veces en muy pocos campos en su carrera y en momentos puntuales, cuando las cosas van muy bien en el club. En Serbia es un poco costumbre en algunos equipos, pero la ovación del otro día me sorprendió. Muy agradecido porque es una sensación extraña para un entrenador. Siento mucha gratitud porque es una señal de que uno está haciendo bien las cosas o de que hay un respeto a la figura del entrenador que hoy en día eso no es muy habitual. P. En Serbia hay un respeto máximo por el entrenador de tu equipo. R. Yo creo que tienen muy interiorizado que la figura del entrenador es la de la persona que tiene que llevar el barco a buen puerto. Tengo la sensación de que el aficionado en Serbia está con el entrenador, igual que está con los jugadores si muestran siempre un compromiso y una profesionalidad. Es algo que aquí en España nos cuesta más ver. También es verdad que allí son extremos para lo bueno y para lo malo. Yo tengo la suerte de estar viviendo ahora una buena situación y estoy muy agradecido de cómo me tratan nuestros aficionados. P. Se lo ha ganado, porque superar el momento en el que llegó... R. Llegué en un momento muy complicado, en una atmósfera muy difícil. En Belgrado y en el Partizan, Zeljko Obradovic es más que el mejor entrenador de Europa de los últimos 25 años. Es mucho más que eso. Que él se fuera era un problema, pero yo no fui allí a sustituir a Zeljko. Fui allí a hacer mi trabajo. Encontré un equipo que estaba con dificultades, había una desunión grande entre lo que era el equipo y la afición, con el equipo no jugando bien... P. ¿Cómo salió de aquello? R. No fue fácil. En el primer mes y medio, los resultados tampoco nos acompañaron. Luego fuimos tomando algunas decisiones. Conseguía que cada día el equipo se uniera más y que jugara más junto. Empezaron a llegar los resultados y empezó a cambiar un poco también la atmósfera. P. No debe de ser una afición sencilla. R. Los aficionados aman al Partizan. Pero sobre todo aman al Partizan si ven que hay una entrega y que se juega en equipo y que se defiende con orgullo la camiseta. Cambiamos la situación y acabamos la temporada de una forma bastante buena, tanto en Euroliga como en la Liga Adriática, aunque perdimos la final contra Dubái, pero ganamos bien en semifinales al Estrella Roja y competimos bien en la final. P. Y ahora, 3-0 en la Euroliga por primera vez en la historia del club. R. Llevamos dos semanas, pero al margen de los resultados, que son muy importantes y nos han dado una cierta tranquilidad, pero esto en dos semanas cambia porque se juegan siete partidos, me quedo sobre todo con la imagen. La de un grupo que está unido, que juega junto, que jugamos sin egos y la gente de momento está contenta. Ahora nuestro trabajo es intentar que sigan estando contentos con su equipo. Pero ya te digo, evidentemente todo el mundo quiere ganar, pero al margen de eso, que es algo que allí ya desde que llegué me dejaron muy claro, sobre todo lo que quieren ver es un equipo comprometido y eso sí que vamos a intentar que sea una obligación para nosotros a lo largo de toda la temporada. P. ¿Se ha disparado la euforia o se asume que el Partizan tiene menos presupuesto y plantilla que la mayoría? R. Las expectativas seguramente con el equipo son las reales. Desde el principio, con el Partizan, las de todo el mundo son bajas o no son las mismas que había en años anteriores seguramente con plantillas con más nombre e incluso con más presupuesto. Evidentemente, ganar influye un poquito a todo el mundo, pero nosotros tenemos los pies en el suelo, sabemos quién somos y sabemos que si no jugamos a casi nuestro cien por cien, es difícil competir en esta Euroliga y compaginarla con la Liga Adriática. Pero también somos conscientes de que somos mejores de lo que muchos piensan. Evidentemente tenemos problemas, somos una de las plantillas más cortas de la competición. Ahora dos jugadores importantes como Derek Willis y Lamar Stevens no están y estamos muy cortos en la rotación. Los chicos están convencidos de que pueden dar guerra y quieren intentar revertir todas esas valoraciones y apreciaciones que se hacen al principio de temporada y que la gente lo valore. De momento están demostrando que tienen el nivel para competir de tú a tú con todo el mundo. De momento, contentos, pero vamos a ver cómo sigue evolucionando esto. P. Empezando por la visita al Real Madrid. ¿Cómo lo ve? R. Yo al Madrid siempre lo veo bien. Yo lo entiendo, ¿eh? Ha perdido tres partidos, sí, pero ha ganado la Supercup. El primer título, que es para lo que está el Madrid, ya lo ha ganado. Ha jugado tres partidos, pero tampoco es normal jugar los tres primeros fuera de casa. Y ha jugado contra tres rivales de presupuesto grande, aspirantes clarísimos a estar en playoffs. Sería casi una sorpresa que los tres equipos contra los que ha perdido el Madrid no estuvieran ahí. Es el Madrid. Y el año pasado perdieron un partido de Euroliga aquí, ¿no? P. Sí, contra el Panathinaikos. R. Pues ahí lo tienes. P. El Madrid se juega mucho más que el Partizan. Empezar 0-4... R. Es un partido importante para ellos, como todos, pero seguro que ese núcleo duro del vestuario va a explicar bien a los nuevos que es un partido que no se puede escapar. Y para nosotros ganar aquí es muy complicado pero venimos a hacer nuestro trabajo, a hacer las cosas que venimos haciendo de la mejor manera. Conociendo la dificultad, intentaremos dar batalla. P. ¿Le sorprendió el fichaje de Pedro Martínez por el Madrid? R. Bueno, el Madrid... El Madrid siempre ficha a los mejores. Y Pedro es uno de los mejores, sin duda alguna. También tenía a uno de los mejores, como era Sergio [Scariolo]. Al final, es la vida del entrenador. Hacen una ACB fantástica, en la que acaban primeros. En Euroliga juegan la Final Four y muchas veces pasa desapercibido, y yo he vivido eso, que se les lesionan los tres pívots. A la gente parece que se le olvida, pero tienes que jugar para ganar sin Tavares, Garuba y Len. Acabaron con un mal gusto. Pero el Madrid siempre ficha a los mejores. Sergio es uno de ellos y Pedro lleva años siendo uno de los mejores. Yo estoy muy contento por él. Siempre ha entrenado grandes equipos y él Valencia es grande también, pero el Madrid es uno de los transatlánticos de Europa.

articles.title: El Real Madrid, obligado a espantar su primera crisis europea
articles.standfirst: Es penúltimo (0-3) tras un inicio que siembra dudas y recibe al invicto Partizan. Si pierde, igualaría la peor racha de su historia en la Euroliga
articles.summary: Es penúltimo (0-3) tras un inicio que siembra dudas y recibe al invicto Partizan. Si pierde, igualaría la peor racha de su historia en la Euroliga
articles.body: Tres derrotas, cero margen para mirar hacia otro lado. El Real Madrid afronta ante el Partizan su primer partido de Euroliga en casa con la necesidad de reaccionar ya. Pedro Martínez sabe que el exigente entorno blanco no entiende de esperas pese a encontrarse en los albores de la temporada: “Yo no soy nadie para pedir paciencia”, dijo en la rueda de prensa previa. Casi sin tiempo para celebrar la conquista de la nueva SuperCup de la Euroliga, el conjunto blanco se ha situado en una situación peliaguda al perder sus tres primeros partidos europeos —Dubai, Efes y Hapoel—, igualando el peor inicio de su historia en la Euroliga. No sirve como eximente el hecho de ser tres derrotas cosechadas a domicilio. El Madrid necesita reaccionar y frenar ya la incertidumbre que ha provocado en el club y entre sus aficionados ese errático inicio. Un nuevo tropiezo, esta vez en casa, podría acarrear consecuencias impredecibles, y certezas desagradables. En caso de perder igualaría la peor racha de su historia en la Euroliga con cuatro derrotas seguidas, algo que le sucedió ya cuatro veces: en la 2002-2003 con Imbroda, en la 2004-05 con Maljkovic, y dos en la campaña 2021-22 bajo la tutela de Laso. Ante este panorama, Pedro Martínez no quiere excusas: “Lo que pido es trabajar en el día a día, hacer las cosas con esfuerzo y estar centrados en hacer lo que depende de nosotros lo mejor posible”, explicó. La palabra paciencia no entra en su discurso. Sí el trabajo y la obligación de mejorar. Martínez, sin embargo, no percibe un vestuario presa del nerviosismo. “No los veo especialmente nerviosos, los veo preocupados y responsabilizados”, aseguró. Le gusta la mentalidad de sus jugadores y destaca que están intentando defender mejor. Pero también admite que las tres derrotas europeas generan “un poco más de intranquilidad”. Una sensación que en el Madrid puede crecer rápido. El entrenador pide separar el resultado del análisis, aunque sabe dónde está. “Los resultados no pueden condicionarlo todo”. Pero tampoco quiere esconderse en un discurso optimista: “No podemos ponernos una venda delante de los ojos”. El Madrid necesita recuperar sensaciones, continuidad y regularidad antes de que el mal comienzo pese más en la grada. Pedro Martínez ya ha empezado a tocar piezas. Reconoce que, a medida que conoce mejor a sus jugadores, detecta cosas que no les encajan y busca variantes, pero descarta un volantazo: no habrá “un cambio radical” en el planteamiento. Necesita encontrar cuanto antes una identidad que todavía está en construcción. En ese contexto el técnico lanzó un mensaje definitivo: “Hay que jugar pensando en el presente”. Ni lamentarse por el 0-3 ni esperar a que la situación se arregle sola. El Madrid necesita una victoria que frene la inquietud antes de que se transforme en nerviosismo.

articles.title: Atlanta Dream y Golden State Valkyries están a un triunfo de las Finales de la WNBA
articles.standfirst: La española Raquel Carrera no jugó en una nueva derrota de las Liberty ante las Dream
articles.summary: La española Raquel Carrera no jugó en una nueva derrota de las Liberty ante las Dream
articles.body: Las Atlanta Dream lucieron la profundidad de su plantilla y ganaron por 101-98 en casa contra las New York Liberty, en las que no jugó la española Raquel Carrera, para tomar ventaja de 2-0 en las semifinales de la WNBA, disputadas al mejor de cinco encuentros, tras imponerse en la prórroga. El equipo de Atlanta defendió el factor cancha y quedó a una victoria de alcanzar las Finales, después de llevarse también el primer encuentro por 92-82. Las Dream afrontaron esta segunda cita sin Allisha Gray, baja por una lesión en la mano, que había abandonado el duelo inaugural del domingo. Jordin Canada y Angel Reese lideraron a las Dream con 23 puntos cada una. Canada repartió 8 asistencias y Reese capturó 7 rebotes. Rhyne Howard añadió 18 puntos y Naz Hillmon, 12 y 8 rebotes. Desde el banquillo, Isobel Borlase aportó 11 puntos, con 3 triples en 5 intentos. Breanna Stewart lideró a las Liberty con 35 puntos, 11 rebotes y 6 asistencias, mientras que Jonquel Jones aportó 21 puntos, 8 rebotes y 4 tapones. La francesa Marine Fauthoux sumó 20 puntos desde el banquillo, con 4 triples en 6 intentos. Fauthoux igualó el marcador a 88 con un triple en el último suspiro del cuarto período para llevar el partido a la prórroga, pero las Liberty no pudieron completar la remontada. La eliminatoria se trasladará ahora a Nueva York, donde el viernes se disputará el tercer partido. Las Golden State Valkyries, franquicia que debutó en la WNBA en 2025, triunfó ganó 81-83 en casa contra Las Vegas Aces, vigentes campeonas, y tomó ventaja de 2-0 en las semifinales de los 'playoffs' para colocarse a una sola victoria de ir a las Finales. Las Valkyries salieron ganadoras en un partido de alta intensidad, lideradas por los 21 puntos de Tiffany Hayes saliendo del banquillo y los 20 de Gabby Williams. Kayla Thornton contribuyó con 16 puntos en una victoria que les permitió imponer la ventaja de campo en los dos primeros duelos de la serie. El equipo de la Bahía tendrá este viernes en Las Vegas su primera oportunidad para volar a las Finales. Las Aces necesitan cambiar la dinámica de la serie. No les bastó con los 24 puntos de A'ja Wilson y con los 19 de Chelsea Gray.
