articles.title: Liberty leave Atlanta mired in timeout controversy, 2-0 semifinal deficit and missed opportunities
articles.summary: The timeout dispute that ended Wednesday's Game 2 will ultimately overshadow the hole the Liberty dug themselves into.
articles.body:
ATLANTA — The physics of a ball shot a millimeter off target flickered hope in the waning seconds of regulation. The New York Liberty came down with it, but their fortune ended there, shining a light on the red herring of a dominant first-round sweep.

And then came the combustion of a logistical rules blunder at the end of overtime in critical semifinals Game 2, initially set in motion by Breanna Stewart instead of her head coach.

The Liberty put Dream forward Angel Reese on the free throw line trailing by one with 4.3 seconds to play, down a game in the best-of-five series. Stewart said that after the first free throw, she asked official Kevin Fahy whether the Liberty had a reset timeout. The TV broadcast caught Stewart turning from the block toward the bench and scorer's table in between Reese's free throws.

"He said, 'I'm going to check at the table,'" Stewart said after the game. "So then he looked to [head official] Fatou [Cissoko-Stephens], and she said no. So then he told me no, like, we don't."

Leonie Fiebich inbounded to Marine Johannes, who tipped it forward to Stewart. She collected it and tossed up an off-balance 32-footer that landed short. The Dream won 101-98 to put the Liberty on the brink; no team has come back from a 2-0 deficit in WNBA postseason history.

"Of course, who knows what would happen at the end of the game, but we would have had hopefully a better shot on goal," Stewart said.

Liberty head coach Chris DeMarco said "same thing," that the officials told multiple staffers they didn't have the reset timeout. Dream head coach Karl Smesko said he thought the Liberty had a timeout left, "but they played it out the way they did." Teams receive one reset timeout in the final two minutes of any overtime period, per the rulebook.

"It is what it is," DeMarco said. "We got to demand more."

The Liberty made an official inquiry to the league regarding the incident, Yahoo Sports confirmed. The official pool report was not conducted inside the arena until two hours after the game ended. Pool reporters submitted specific questions while Stewart, DeMarco and Jonquel Jones were still on the podium.

Per the pool report, Cissoko-Stephens said there "was no communication with the officials or the team."

"Stewart was standing behind referee Fahy when he confirmed with his partner between Reese's penalty free throws that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," per the pool report.

"Available timeouts are tracked by scorer's table and statistical staff. Teams are responsible for managing and tracking their timeout usage throughout the game. Officials may confirm the status of timeouts with the table when necessary, but they do not officially track timeouts."

Undoubtedly, the controversy will overshadow the hole the Liberty dug themselves into.

"I think this sounds like a big drama, but I don't think that's the reason why we lost," Fiebich, who stepped into the starting lineup in the 2024 postseason run, told a small group of reporters outside the locker room. "I think it's, of course, unfortunate, but I think we could have won before that. Didn't let it come that far."

But had the German national star ever been in such a situation where there was confusion over whether or not there was a timeout?

Serendipity landed in the Liberty's laps over and over again on Wednesday night in Atlanta. Allisha Gray, the Dream's leading scorer, was ruled out the day prior with a hand injury. Stewart, whose perimeter game has faded in recent years, tied a season-high two 3-pointers in the first five minutes. The Liberty's challenge of a sixth foul call on Jones, their 6-foot-9 center, was deemed successful with 4:41 to play.

The backcourt handled the ball pressure better. They were in it despite still giving up 28 points off 17 turnovers, and nearly setting the record for best field goal percentage in a playoff loss . Marine Fauthoux, a WNBA rookie from France, drained a 3-pointer to tie it with 10.3 seconds on the clock.

And back to that ball off the hands of a driving Rhyne Howard that flat-lined the heartbeats of an entire arena. The leather pinged the back of the basket and rolled around the entire rim. It popped out toward the glass. It sat on the iron. It fell into Jones' waiting hands.

The buzzer sounded; the basket light flashed. The arena groaned. Five more minutes of life to flip the series and the season.

The beginning of the end of the Liberty's season might have ultimately hinged on a no-call in transition when Angel Reese grabbed at Breanna Stewart in a five-point game. Or Fauthoux's 25-foot stepback 3 attempt at the end of the shot clock that bounced out in a one-point game. Or the bad-pass turnover by Jones in a three-point game with 2:05 in regulation.

Sabrina Ionescu told reporters outside the locker room that she told the team the loss was her fault. Fiebich said they all feel the responsibility.

"I think we all f***** up at some stage throughout the game, especially late," Fiebich said.

There is no shortage of choices. Not in Game 2 and not season-wide. Talent and past experiences can only take a team so far. For the 2026 New York Liberty, it seems inevitable that the journey stops short of the Finals. Empty possessions at the end, a lead finally in hand, ultimately led to a game that hinged on he-said, she-said.

The Liberty have a roster stacked with talent, boasting the second-most returners of any squad's opening day roster, including four starters who won a championship together two years ago. They are now at risk of being swept in stunning fashion in the WNBA semifinals, led by a first-year head coach who was supposed to take them farther than their first-round exit a year ago.

Technically, he did. They're still playing, instead of watching the semis from their couches. It's unlikely they'll be saying that much longer. The turnaround is tight. Game 3 is on Friday in New York, where the Liberty believe they can defend their own enthusiastic crowd the way the Dream have done in Atlanta.

The moment that cracked open the controversy will be what lingers. The Liberty are squandering another all-time great, MVP-caliber season by Stewart, an illustrious winner fresh off a fourth FIBA World Cup championship.

"It's so many, so many plays that kind of led to this, but…" Stewart said in response to the first question of the postgame press conference. One of the league's greatest players stopped speaking, turned to her right, and stared at her first-time head coach.

"Am I the one saying it?" Stewart asked, pointing at herself before turning to DeMarco beside her. "Or you?"

"What's that?" the longtime NBA assistant coach answered with a slight shrug. Stewart took a quick, deep breath, flipped her hand upward, turned back to the mic, and once again this lost season took the lead.

"This is not blaming the refs, but when I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end, and they tell us no, and then we leave the game with a reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart said, clearly carrying over the feeling to the postgame podium.

At the other end of the short table sat Jones. DeMarco, sandwiched between two former MVPs and WNBA champions, sat unemotive on the brink of elimination.

"Like, yeah, OK, I kind of got a good look at the end, but would just love to have some clarity on that situation as well," Stewart finished.

articles.summary: Los blancos buscan su primera victoria en la Liga regular
articles.body: Resulta curioso pensar que el primer equipo ganador de un título a nivel europeo, el Real Madrid, aún no se haya estrenado en la Liga regular cuando se dispone a afrontar la cuarta jornada. Pero es así, el 0-3 del Madrid es tan sorprendente como real y está causando mucha inquietud en el equipo blanco. Para tratar que esa inquietud no se transforme en nerviosismo y algo más es por lo que el equipo de Pedro Martínez necesita ganar al Partizan de Belgrado en lo que será su primera partido europeo en el Movistar Arena. Ya debutó en casa ante el Unicaja en Liga Endesa, pero no había sido anfitrión aún en Euroliga, así que el partido llega en plena necesidad blanca por la victoria. Si tenemos en cuenta los precedentes, el Partizan es un buen cliente para el Madrid. Los de Martínez han ganado sus últimos cinco duelos ante los serbios incluyendo los dos de la temporada pasada. Pero resulta que el equipo que entrena Joan Peñarroya ha tenido un arranque fabuloso y es uno de los cuatro equipos que están arriba con un 3-0 de salida (junto a Panathinaikos, Valencia y Fenerbahce). Pedro Martínez, que no podrá contar con Gabi Deck por un problema en el hombre, decía sobre la especie de crisis europea del Madrid: "Yo no soy nadie para pedir paciencia. Lo que pido es trabajar en el día a día, hacer las cosas con esfuerzo y que estemos centrados en hacer las cosas que dependen de nosotros lo mejor posible". Me gusta que están intentando defender mejor y que sean conscientes de que tenemos que mejorar. Hay cosas positivas y cosas a mejorar, pero si hubiéramos ganado, también". articles.title: La respuesta de NBA y FIBA al no de la Euroliga: NBA Europa sigue adelante
articles.standfirst: Ambos estamentos emiten un comunicado tras la decisión de la Asamblea General de la Euroliga
articles.summary: Ambos estamentos emiten un comunicado tras la decisión de la Asamblea General de la Euroliga
articles.body: LA NBA y a FIBA rompieron su silencio tras la Asamblea General de la Euroliga en el Lago Como y la desestimación por parte de los 13 equipos propietarios de una oferta para lograr un frente unido. NBA y FIBA emitieron este jueves un comunicado en respuesta a esa decisión en el que, por encima de todo, se desprende que ambas entidades seguirán adelante con el proyecto de NBA Europa con o sin la Euroliga. Aunque la idea de los 13 equipos es seguir negociando, NBA y FIBA aseguran en su comunicado que "siguen comprometidas a seguir adelante con una nueva liga masculina profesional en Europa". Aunque el comunicado es claro, también menciona que el escenario ideal sería un acuerdo entre las tres partes para "unificar el ecosistema del baloncesto europeo". En el Lago Como los equipos desestimaron la oferta de la NBA, pero a pesar de que algunos equipos querían dejar de negociar, la mayoría se inclinó por seguir escuchando a la otra parte y mantener la vía de la negociación abierta. Este es el comunicado completo de NBA y FIBA: "Una asociación entre la Euroliga, la FIBA y la NBA para unificar el ecosistema europeo del baloncesto desbloquearía el enorme potencial del juego en toda Europa en beneficio de clubes, jugadores y, lo más importante, aficionados. La NBA y la FIBA siguen comprometidas a seguir adelante con una nueva liga masculina profesional en Europa y ayudar a construir un ecosistema de baloncesto más fuerte y sostenible junto con socios que comparten nuestra visión de crecimiento, oportunidad y los principios fundamentales del modelo deportivo europeo".

articles.title: Sports media outlet considers Sophie Cunningham more polarizing than Megan Rapinoe
articles.summary: Sophie Cunningham faces calls to leave the Indiana Fever, but the double standard with Megan Rapinoe's activism reveals a deeper media bias.
articles.body: This week, a columnist for The New York Times’ The Athletic called for the Indiana Fever to part ways with Sophie Cunningham. "She’s too turbulent to be paired with Caitlin Clark," Candace Buckner wrote in the headline. "[I]f the Fever ever want to go back to being a basketball team again and follow the lead of rivals openly clashing with the forces trying to hijack their league, then Cunningham has to go," she added. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The column portrays Cunningham as an outspoken agitator whose growing profile has become a distraction for the Fever. As evidence, Buckner cited comments Cunningham made earlier this year in an ESPN article about trans athletes competing against girls. For background, Cunningham said she "loves" all communities but believes it is important to "protect young girls" and that they "shouldn’t have to go against biological men" in sports. WNBA players and members of the media subsequently framed those comments as transphobic. We emphasize that particular comment because, beyond it, Cunningham has hardly been the political lightning rod her detractors depict her as. THE ATHLETIC COLUMN URGING INDIANA FEVER TO PART WAYS WITH SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM DRAWS WIDESPREAD CRITICISM Most of Cunningham’s public persona consists of playing basketball, dancing on TikTok, and trying on outfits. One could argue that her personality and attractive appearance have contributed to her supposed polarizing status. As Sydney Sweeney could attest, a certain corner of the media and social media seems uniquely irritated by attractive blonde women who refuse to apologize for it. The second-most controversial thing Cunningham has said recently was telling A’ja Wilson to "grow up" after Wilson charged toward a courtside fan who pointed at her during a playoff game. Teammates had to restrain Wilson before arena security intervened. And yet, The New York Times’ sports vertical has seen enough. It's time for the Fever to move on, the reporter declared. One might find The Athletic’s position more persuasive if it were consistent. But it's not. It never has been. Consider soccer player Megan Rapinoe. Unlike Cunningham, Rapinoe spent years making politics central to her public identity. She knelt during the national anthem and later said she would probably never sing it again. She claimed during the 2019 World Cup that she was "not going to the f---ing White House" if President Donald Trump invited the team. She publicly supported Democratic candidates, including Hillary Clinton and Elizabeth Warren. She described Trump as "sexist," "misogynistic," "small-minded," "racist," and "not a good person." Rapinoe also condemned the Supreme Court’s 2022 decision overturning Roe v. Wade as "sad and cruel," became a prominent supporter of Black Lives Matter, repeatedly advocated for transgender women to compete in women’s sports, and once dismissed concerns about competitive fairness as "total bullshit." More recently, she called for traditional WNBA media to make room for people who "understand queer culture." MEGAN RAPINOE SAYS WOMEN'S SPORTS ARE FACING 'REGRESSION' OF 'EQUAL RIGHTS' IN NEW KAMALA HARRIS INTERVIEW After tearing her Achilles in the final match of her career, Rapinoe said afterward that the injury was "proof that there isn’t" a God. Whatever one thinks of those positions, no reasonable person could describe Rapinoe as reluctant to inject politics, religion, and contentious social issues into sports. Yet the sports media never mounted a campaign for Rapinoe’s teams to part ways with her because she was too "turbulent." Her activism was not treated as an impediment to her team getting "back to being a soccer team." Quite the opposite. Rapinoe became one of the most celebrated athletes in American sports media, in no small part because of her willingness to speak about politics – the right side of politics, that is. Her activism was incorporated into her public brand and routinely presented as evidence of courage and leadership. That is the double standard. The sports media rarely treats athletes who espouse liberal or progressive political views as problematic, even when those views are provocative, divisive, or factually incorrect. The latter is quite common. Rapinoe is not the only example. LeBron James has spent years commenting on presidential politics, policing, and race all in favor of Democratic positions. Colin Kaepernick turned an anthem protest into the defining feature of his public identity. Sue Bird, Breanna Stewart and Natasha Cloud have routinely spoken about progressive political causes. Steve Kerr has addressed topics ranging from gun control to presidential politics and supported Kamala Harris for president on stage at the Democratic National Convention in 2024. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE We can't find a single article from The Athletic, New York Times, ESPN, The Ringer, Washington Post, or CBS Sports critical of any of those statements. Meanwhile, the same reporters and commentators treat Cunningham saying that girls deserve protected athletic categories, Harrison Butker promoting traditional marriage, or Jaxson Dart introducing Trump on stage as grounds for condemnation or even action from their teams and business partners. See, the perspectives of many sports writers are shaped by the bubble in which they operate. In their world — virtual newsrooms, Bluesky, Threads, Instagram and sports blogs — saying that men and women possess meaningful biological differences can qualify as an outrageous offense. Outside that bubble, the position is decidedly mainstream. National polling consistently shows that between 75-80% of voting Americans oppose biological males competing in women’s sports. The disconnect between the sports media and the average American is stark To one group, Sophie Cunningham is a combustible firebrand and Megan Rapinoe is a courageous activist. To the other, Cunningham is expressing a common-sense position shared by most of the country, while Rapinoe is a divisive political figure. Unfortunately, the people with the largest megaphones in sports media overwhelmingly represent the smaller of those two groups. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Buckner knew her column about Sophie Cunningham would score her the culture war points she seeks. However, its premise also illustrates the very ideological hypocrisy that has alienated much of the public from the press. She finds Cunningham "turbulent." The Fever, its fans, and most of America do not.

articles.title: Ranking the 25 Best Fantasy Basketball Team Names We Could Find
articles.summary: Congratulations to all the procrastinators waiting to name their fantasy basketball teams until just before the start of the 2026-27 NBA season. You have delayed your decision long enough to pull one from this list.
articles.body:
Congratulations to all the procrastinators waiting to name their fantasy basketball teams until just before the start of the 2026-27 NBA season. You have delayed your decision long enough to pull one from this list.

Building this compilation was a labor of love and self-loathing. Hours upon hours were spent scouring the internet. Past and present lists were read. I have seen things on Reddit I can't unsee; searched for the meaning of team names I didn't understand and found results I can't unsearch; and crafted options of my own that I'm neither proud of nor able to take back.

All of it was done in service of what you see here: a comprehensive ranking of the catchiest, cleverest, funniest and/or cheesiest fantasy names for this season.

Only two rules guided these results. First and foremost, none of last year's selections are eligible for inclusion. While I'm not sure we can top gems like "Sir, This Is A Wemby's," we're starting from scratch anyway.

Second, each name must relate back to a current player or NBA figure/storyline. Apologies to anyone who stumbled across this page looking for Dirk Nowitzki-inspired phallic puns.

Your answer to this play-on-words question better be Tyrese Haliburton.

Then again, if it's Jeff Halliburton, I have nothing but respect for your knowledge of obscure 1970s third-round picks who lasted only two seasons at the NBA level.

Are you a Portland Trail Blazers fan who also drafts and runs your make-believe squad like a tactless penny-pinching Texas-based private equity and investment firm founder who (likely) can't write his own "I'm not cheap; just smarter than you" email release without asking Grok to adopt the tone of Claude impersonating ChatGPT?

Well then, woooo buddy, do I have a fantasy team name for you!

In Memphis, you silly goose! That’s where the Detroit Pistons shipped Isaiah “Beef Stew” Stewart this offseason.

If you are old enough to remember this iconic Wendy's commercial and still playing fantasy basketball, here's a free piece of life advice: Never change. Like, ever.

Also, "Where's the Keefe?!" is a fine alternative. But the answer gets awkward if you think the Washington Wizards' current science project of a roster ends with head coach Brian Keefe receiving the boot.

Except, of course, for Caleb Wilson. Who actually matters more.

Unless you aren't aware that Matas Buzelis is a third-year forward who plays for the Chicago Bulls.

In which case this will go over your head.

Off the top of my head, aside from turning Cam Whitmore into a thiccer Peyton Watson, there's plenty more Nikola Jokić can do. That list includes but is not limited to:

Cloning himself to finally solve the Denver Nuggets' backup center conundrum

Loaning money to Kroenke Sports & Entertainment so that they can afford to spend $4 billion on the Los Angeles Angels and avoid cutting Denver's payroll at the expense of helpful talent

Threatening to demand a trade to the Los Angeles Lakers or US Equestrian Eventing National Championship League if the Nuggets don't deal Cleveland's 2031 first-rounder for a roster upgrade

Screaming " You just got Serbed! " after every assist

Petitioning the NBA to relocate the Minnesota Timberwolves to the Eastern Conference as part of its expansion plans

Paying for head coach David Adelman to attend cotillion

See? There's plenty he's still not doing to help this team!

Sorry, but if Jakob Poeltl has never dressed up as Donatello, Raphael, Leonardo or Michelangelo for Halloween, World Turtle Day (May 23), International Ninja Day (December 5) or just your average, run-of-the-mill Tuesday night, the Toronto Raptors should consider waiving him and stretching his contract.

This is a great name for those whose league includes someone predisposed to reading AI-generated summaries of books and movies, then discussing their plot points and societal messaging as though they were an expert critic.

Remember: Everything in life is a subtweet.

Are we nodding toward Atlanta Hawks rookie Zuby Ejiofor? Or is this a subtle expansion on Ivica Zubac's "Zu" nickname?

As long as the original Scooby Do o theme song is playing on a nonstop loop in your head, the answer doesn't matter.

Get your mind out of the gutter. This is an expansion-draft prediction about Collin Sexton.

We should all have nothing but respect for our bald king, and for anyone who takes a razor to the hair-recession battle. [Sobs into my own retreating hairline.]

15. Klay It Ain't So, Dray Will Not Go, Turn the Light Years Off, Curry Me Home

For the millennial fantasy ballers whose leagues don't have character limits and who appreciate long-winded wordplay.

Also, and this is important : Na-na, na-na, na-na, na-na, na, na.

Normally, you would want the answer to be "do."

Exactly two preseason games into Aday Mara's career, though, I'm taking the latter .

Why yes, we have! He's just out of frame , ready for a crack at his own championship-fueling tip-in if yours fails.

On a related note: There's not enough "Anunoby" as "anybody" wordplay in our lives. Let's all agree, as a family, to change that.

This name gets a boost for its double meaning. It can refer to LeBron James' current form of daily transportation as well as his parenting of Philadelphia 76ers teammates.

Sure, NBA play-by-play legend Mike Breen has already walked back his story about LeBron scolding Joel Embiid for not having a free-of-charge chartered helicopter at his disposal. But as Dr. Gene Beresin wrote at MassGeneralBrigham.org: "A helicopter parent excessively monitors and micromanages most areas of their child's life."

If that doesn't describe LeBron's adult-in-the-room leadership style and also the vibe of his locker room Spotify playlist (ads included), what does?

Not to be political, but...Jordan Poole deserves to be the No. 1 option for the New Orleans Pelicans.

Failing that, he at least shouldn't have to drink Gatorade with green or mustard-yellow algae particles in it.

This is a terrific incorporation of Ausar Thompson's name. And it will be topical any time he Eurosteps in transition .

Alternative-seeking fantasy ballers may also consider "Dancin' with the Sarrs." But it felt less accurate with Olivier Sarr currently playing in Europe.

No, this ranking is not a paid sponsorship by Degree . "DeoDurant" is simply an awesome and unique integration of Kevin Durant's name.

Truth be told, we could bump this a few rungs up the ladder if "Kevin DeoDurant" wasn't so hard to say 10 times fast. Or if he didn't leave every team he's ever played for with fouler-smelling locker room vibes.

Emphasis on vibes here. I'm sure KD himself smells perfectly lovely.

Maybe you consider this a rebuke to people overlooking Luka Dončić and the Los Angeles Lakers after the team's summer spending spree.

Or maybe you view this as an eventual plea from Luka to Nikola Jokić, begging him to get Denver to carve out 2028 cap space because the Lakers burned through financial flexibility and assets in a determined attempt to trap themselves inside mediocrity.

It doesn't matter, really. Art is whatever you want it to be.

With Kon Knueppel nursing a hamstring strain, doomsdayers might go with "Wrath of Kon's Hamstring." Not us, though.

Instead, we choose to celebrate the clean reimagining of a Star Trek film yours truly has never seen.

I have no idea whether Deni Avdija is into superstitions . Or black cats. Or voodoo dolls. Or even new sensations.

But I do know that the Blazers watching what he did last season and then coming to the decision that pairing him with Ja Morant would be a good idea qualifies as a crazy lifestyle choice.

Mostly, though, "Livin' Avdija Loco" just sounds cool when using the correct pronunciation of Deni's surname. As an added bonus, it also lets us avoid a played-out Denny's reference.

This name rules not only because it's a Spider-Man callback, but because it doesn't have to be about Victor Wembanyama.

It could be an ode to Alex Sarr or Zach Edey, Walker Kessler or Anthony Davis, Rudy Gobert or Donovan Clingan. The list goes on.

On a totally unrelated note: It's about Wemby.

"Ball don't lie!" is an irreverently iconic phrase with a fascinating origin story . While "Ball don't drive!" is an homage to its legacy, it's also rooted in real life.

Anthony Edwards has apparently "assigned" or at least given his personal driver's info to new teammate LaMelo Ball. So, LaMelo may quite literally not be driving.

Shout-out to Ant for helping his new teammate get around Minnesota.

The medulla oblongata is a part of your nervous system that has a whole host of responsibilities. Handling automatic processes—or as the Cleveland Clinic puts it , "things that your body often does without you having to think about them"—is among its most important functions.

Now, this doesn't mean the medulla is responsible for Joe Mazzulla's instinctual need to talk like Batman or watch The Town on a tri-hourly basis. But dammit if "Mazzulla Oblongata" doesn't sound cool as hell.

Apart from sounding pretty rad, the beauty of "Chetflix Originals" is its versatility.

Two-handed blocks? That's a Chetflix Original. Pre-game moonball shots that go straight up in the air rather than toward the basket? That's a Chetflix Original.

Starring in a cringey wireless commercial ? Not really a Chetflix Original. But sporting a haircut that looks like Dax Shepard trying to be Theo Von? Now that is a Chetflix Original.

A Victor Wembanyama-inspired name takes the top spot for the second year running. It is not by design.

"Infinity Wembeyond" just sort of rolls off the tongue, looks badass written out, and quite frankly, encapsulates the overall sentiment.

Nothing you say about Wemby is technically hyperbole. Think he'll average 30 points, 15 rebounds and four blocks this season? I mean, he probably won't, but we shouldn't rule it out.

Do you have him winning MVP, Defensive Player of the Year, Most Improved Player and Clutch Player of the Year? Though I wouldn't endorse betting on it, there are worse ways to spend your money. (Like on the Sacramento Kings' title odds.)

Dan Favale is a National NBA Writer for Bleacher Report. Follow him on Bluesky ( @danfavale ), and subscribe to the Hardwood Knocks podcast, co-hosted by Bleacher Report's Grant Hughes .

articles.title: The 5 NBA Players With Most To Prove This Season
articles.summary: Life as an NBA player is a constant cycle of success and skepticism.
articles.body:
Life as an NBA player is a constant cycle of success and skepticism.

Arrive as a highly touted prospect, and you have to show you can do it at the next level. Establish yourself as an All-Star, and everyone questions whether you can sustain it. Dominate through your prime, and then quiet the doubters calling for your decline.

It's an exhausting existence, but it's better than the alternative of never succeeding in the first place.

Here, we'll take a look at a handful of players who face serious questions during the upcoming NBA season. All of them have enjoyed loads of career triumphs, earned tons of money and accumulated awards.

And all of them have plenty left to prove.

Jalen Duren would have made this list based on either last year's shocking playoff disappearance or the offseason's most drawn-out and acrimonious contract negotiation alone.

That he enters 2026-27 with both of those factors dogging him makes his inclusion a no-brainer.

Despite earning an All-NBA nod last season, Duren did not receive a maximum contract from the Detroit Pistons.

According to Dan Feldman of Dunc'd On, the 22-year-old became the first player to earn an All-Star selection while on a rookie-scale contract and then sign a below-max deal immediately afterward. His five-year, $200 million agreement falls well short of the maximum he sought.

Clearly, the big man's postseason struggles were a concern. We also learned during the negotiating process that Detroit was unconvinced about his work ethic. The Athletic's Sam Amick reported that the weight clause—which the Pistons initially wanted in the deal, and which annoyed Duren—stemmed from concerns about whether he was "disciplined enough in the gym to truly earn this kind of payday."

Anyone who watched Duren flop in the playoffs is right to doubt him, and his own team clearly didn't believe what he did during the regular season was a sign of things to come.

After all this, the Pistons are still invested in Duren as if he's the second-best player on a contender. All he has to do to justify that status is dispel concerns that he won't work hard and can't produce in the playoffs.

Job No. 1 for Walker Kessler will be staying healthy, something he definitely didn't do in playing just five games a season ago. His 58 appearances in 2024-25 won't cut it either.

That's because job No. 2 for the Los Angeles Lakers' new starting center is justifying the massive price the team paid to get him. Kessler can't do that unless he's on the floor for at least 70 games.

Clearly desperate to appease Luka Dončić, LA sent the Utah Jazz two unprotected first-round picks and two swaps—all for the privilege of paying Kessler $130 million over four years.

Kessler didn't have a hand in the Lakers' decision-making, but it'll be up to him to prove they were in their right minds when they gave up the kind of trade package it usually takes to land a true superstar.

Never once an All-Star or All-Defensive performer, the 25-year-old center has to feature prominently on the short list of DPOY candidates while lifting the Lakers' defense near top-10 territory. That's an unfair ask, but the Lakers treated Kessler as if he were the missing piece in a championship puzzle.

If he doesn't perform like one, the Lakers will look ridiculous for spending so recklessly. Even worse, it might make Dončić realize he doesn't have a chance to win big in Los Angeles.

Minnesota is betting on LaMelo Ball. Charlotte, meanwhile, decided to move on immediately after the most positively impactful season of his career.

Charlotte may have extricated itself from the Ball business for any number of reasons. Most logically, it decided to sell high on an injury-prone player whom it minute-managed to 72 appearances after he averaged just 33 games over the previous three seasons.

Ball's long-term contract cost and defensive limitations also raised questions about his fit as the Hornets' cornerstone.

In Minnesota, Ball will have every opportunity to prove Charlotte wrong. To do that, he'll need to stay healthy, elevate the Wolves' attack, make a consistent effort on defense and demonstrate greater maturity off the floor.

If he can manage all that, the Hornets may come to regret their decision. If he can't, Charlotte will be lauded for getting out while the getting was good.

NBA Players with the All-Time Most Career Earnings💰

Starting his fifth season, collecting a rookie-scale-max salary for the first time and leading an Orlando Magic team that has already made major trades and changed head coaches, Paolo Banchero is out of excuses.

That's a slightly unfair framing of the situation, as Banchero didn't build the Magic roster or pay himself. But he's the guy in Orlando—the No. 1 overall pick in 2022 and basically the No. 1 option ever since.

The 23-year-old has been an inefficient volume scorer throughout his career, one whose obvious physical gifts suit him for alpha status but whose ball-stopping ways often seemed responsible for Orlando's struggles to score.

Far from a bust, Banchero totes career averages of 22.3 points, 7.4 rebounds and 4.8 assists. He looked dominant in the 2025 playoffs and already has an All-Star nod on his resumé.

That said, expectations for Banchero are high. Orlando has invested heavily in Franz Wagner and Jalen Suggs, traded for Desmond Bane and replaced Jamahl Mosley with Sean Sweeney amid reports of tension between Banchero and his former coach.

It's not hard to guess which lever the Magic will pull next if they remain unsatisfied with the team's performance. If tweaking the variables doesn't work, Orlando will have to consider whether Banchero, the constant, was actually the problem all along.

De'Aaron Fox could have been forgiven for feeling a little dizzy after the 2026 NBA Finals.

That kind of career whiplash takes some getting used to.

The San Antonio Spurs traded for Fox as their theoretical second fiddle to Victor Wembanyama in February 2025 and promptly handed him a four-year, $229 million max extension that offseason.

Smash cut to an injured Fox underperforming in the Finals while rookie teammate Dylan Harper effectively announced himself as a superstar in waiting, and everything is different.

Now, Fox is viewed as duplicative in San Antonio—or, even worse, as standing in the way of better, younger and cheaper options. Harper and Stephon Castle are the Spurs' backcourt of the future, and however much head coach Mitch Johnson might say he wants to play all three guards together, it's pretty easy to see that flipping Fox for a high-priced forward could unlock an elevated version of the team.

This seems like an appropriate time to note that Fox is a very good player—one whose failures in the Finals owed largely to an ankle injury. That said, he's never proved himself worthy of a max salary, never led his previous team to meaningful playoff success and could quickly find himself on the trade block if his younger teammates ascend as expected.

Fox is basically playing for his job, which is a wild turn of events given how recently he was viewed as the Spurs' missing piece.

Stats courtesy of NBA.com , Basketball Reference and Cleaning the Glass . Salary info via Spotrac .

articles.title: Sarah Spain calls Fever GM 'defensive' for defending fans, but has plenty to say to her own critics
articles.summary: Sarah Spain assumed Indiana Fever fans had been ejected from WNBA games, but GM Amber Cox's security records challenged that entire narrative.
articles.body: Sarah Spain thought Indiana Fever fans had been removed from games for violating the WNBA's fan code of conduct. Then general manager Amber Cox said no fans had been removed from the team's home games this season, citing the organization's security records. That news surprised Spain ... but it didn't stop her from criticizing Cox for sounding "defensive" in her rebuttal. Well, wouldn't you be defensive if people kept trashing your fans and you had information that contradicted what they were saying? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Spain certainly understands wanting to defend herself. When she didn't like one of my columns, she devoted part of her podcast to complaining about it. But when Cox pushes back on the media, Spain has a problem with her tone. Cox challenges the media's portrayal of Fever fans "The attacks on our fan base have no basis in reality, and they need to stop, especially with members of the media," Cox said during her season-ending news conference. She clarified that she was referring to media who hadn't attended a game at Gainbridge Fieldhouse. LEFT-WING SPORTS HOST SARAH SPAIN LAUNCHES DISGUSTING PERSONAL SMEAR OF SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM Cox acknowledged that bad behavior happens and said anyone crossing the line, online or in an arena, should be held accountable. But she also had information about the fans actually attending her team's games. "We did not have one fan pointed out by a player who violated the WNBA code of conduct this season. Not one fan was removed from a game," Cox said. "We take this really seriously, and that is backed up by our security stats and the lived experiences of countless fans who we host at every game." "To be characterized in such a broad stroke is not fair," she added. On a recent episode of her podcast, Spain credited Cox for providing that information. Perhaps more telling, though, is what Spain had assumed before hearing Cox's comments: "I thought that there had been at least one incident where fans were removed and it had been clear that there had been an incident," Spain said. Which incident? What did the fan do? Where did she get that impression? Spain didn't identify the incident she had in mind or where she had heard about it, leaving listeners unable to check it against Cox's statement. Instead, Spain argued that Cox needed to acknowledge why players and visiting fans might feel there was a problem. So, even after presenting information that challenged the accusations against her fans, Cox still owed the people making those accusations a more accommodating response, according to Spain. Later, while agreeing with guest Jordan Robinson's criticism, Spain said: "The defensiveness as opposed to the openness. Not we want to fix why people have the wrong idea. Instead, people have the wrong idea and we're mad at them." Yes, Sarah. People can have the wrong idea, and the people they're talking about can be mad about it. Especially when those people have been repeatedly called racists and bigots. Cox had already called for accountability for actual misconduct and cited the team's security records to defend her fans. Spain still wanted her to be more accommodating, but Cox's job isn't to make the people trashing her fans feel better about being challenged. What happens when the allegations don't hold up? There's a bit of a Mandela Effect going on with the left-wing media and Fever fans. Allegations get remembered as proven misconduct, and fans who chose to leave get remembered as having been kicked out. In May 2025, the WNBA investigated allegations of racist fan behavior during a Fever-Sky game. The league reviewed audio and video and gathered information from fans, team personnel and arena staff. The WNBA concluded that it could "not substantiate" the allegations. I wrote about ESPN's coverage while that investigation was still underway because commentators were plowing ahead with the narrative that Fever fans are racist without waiting for any evidence. ESPN’S FAVORITE INSIDER ACCIDENTALLY EXPLAINED WHY MOST AMERICANS DON’T TRUST THE MEDIA This year, in August, Las Vegas Aces guard Jackie Young complained about a Fever fan during a game, and security pulled him aside. The fan voluntarily chose to leave and the Fever later explained that security found no code-of-conduct violation and hadn't ejected him. But by then, media have already described the encounter as an ejection. People who missed the Fever's explanation were getting the wrong account of what happened. Then there was A'ja Wilson's confrontation with a Fever fan during last week's playoff game. The Fever said security spoke with the fan and witnesses, found no code-of-conduct violation and didn't remove the fan from the arena. Spain did distinguish that encounter from other incidents involving alleged racist rhetoric and also said individual encounters should be assessed separately. OK, then apply that to the broader accusations against Fever fans. Which incidents support them, and which have been repeated so often that people just assume they happened? Online trolls posting hateful comments on social media don't establish how the crowd at Gainbridge behaves. Nor does a player confronting or complaining about a fan establish that the fan crossed the line. Yet, the media loves to immediately rush to the defense of these WNBA players without evidence. Spain was surprised by Cox's account of the team's security record. I'd have liked to hear more about why she had a different impression and less about whether Cox sounded sufficiently open-minded while correcting it. My suspicion is that she gets her news almost exclusively from left-wing outlets, so she hears plenty about the accusations against Fever fans and a lot less about the reporting that challenges them. For what it's worth, Spain says she doesn't use X anymore, opting instead to post and read posts on Bluesky. Do with that information what you will. Spain knows how to defend herself In August, I argued that Spain's preferred approach to WNBA media sounded more like public relations than journalism. My commentary was based entirely on her own words, not something I invented out of thin air. Spain wasn't pleased. On her Sept. 16 show, she referred to "my own former colleague who now works at that outlet" before discussing coverage of her comments about WNBA media credentials. That was me. We both worked at ESPN, the outlet she was talking about is OutKick and the column she described was mine. "They reworded that as me saying real media, which is just PR for the players," she complained. Then she accused the outlet of "asking the same question 8,000 times in order to keep doing the same story over and over for clicks." Careful, Sarah, because that sounds awfully defensive to me. You should show more openness and ask why I had those thoughts rather than getting mad that I had them. Am I doing this right? FORMER ESPN RADIO HOST SARAH SPAIN REFERRED TO J.D. VANCE AS A 'DEMON' AND 'THE DEVIL' And that Sept. 16 episode had another example of Spain finding plenty of room for nuance when the subject was Sarah Spain. While criticizing Sydney Sweeney's Novig ad, she recalled starting her own on-camera career in cut-up jerseys and push-up bras. Her response to people using those pictures against her? "Hate the game, not the player." But we're not done. She also defended her "publicity stunt" to get Super Bowl tickets. In 2007, Spain posted an eBay ad offering to be someone's date to the game, complete with a photo of herself in a Chicago Bears cheerleader costume, cleavage on full display. Spain called it "this really clever viral idea that ended up getting me tickets to the game and all these connections." She was "using the system," she explained, and later used those contacts to get jobs. So, Spain's defense was that women trying to break into sports faced fewer opportunities then and she basically had no choice but to try and use sex appeal to further her career. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE But, when discussing Sweeney, Spain complained that "we're back to this bulls--t where if a woman is involved in speaking to men, she should be naked." I'd have more patience for that lecture if she extended Sweeney a little of the generosity she demands when discussing her own career. And I'd have more patience for her criticism of Cox if she hadn't demonstrated, at length, how much she values the chance to defend herself. Spain has different rules for her own critics Spain was still talking about her critics in a more recent episode, during a conversation with influencer Coach Jackie. She described outlets as "so obsessed with what I'm doing" and said: "Like, the people who suck, I don't care how many stories they write about me, but I don't want to let the story get bigger because of it." She's certainly keeping up with the coverage. She knew enough about my column to dispute its argument on her show. That's fine, but it makes her reaction to Cox harder to take seriously. She knows exactly why someone might want to challenge a story about them, especially if they believe the story is unfair or unfounded (though my column was neither). Spain has talked about letting "garbage content" die in darkness. I take the opposite view: sunlight is the best disinfectant. If she makes a bad argument about Fever fans, I'm going to write about it. Her deciding that the people criticizing her radical opinions "suck" isn't much of a rebuttal. Cox gave Spain a reason to revisit what she believed about Fever fans. Spain acknowledged the information, then got back to criticizing the Fever's response. I'd like to know what, if anything, would make her reconsider the coverage instead. If Spain is worried about disappointing people who share her views, how willing is she to tell them something they don't want to hear?

articles.title: NBA, FIBA 'Remain Committed' to European League After Proposal Rejected by EuroLeague Owners
articles.summary: Despite EuroLeague owners rejecting a merger offer this week, the NBA and FIBA announced Thursday that they are moving forward with plans to create a new NBA Europe league.
articles.body:
Despite EuroLeague owners rejecting a merger offer this week, the NBA and FIBA announced Thursday that they are moving forward with plans to create a new NBA Europe league.

In a joint statement , the NBA and FIBA said, "A partnership between the EuroLeague, FIBA and the NBA to unify the European basketball ecosystem would unlock the game's enormous potential across Europe for the benefit of clubs, players and, most importantly, fans. The NBA and FIBA remain committed to moving forward with a new professional men's league in Europe and helping build a stronger, more sustainable basketball ecosystem alongside partners who share our vision of growth, opportunity and the core principles of the European sports model."

Per ESPN's Brian Windhorst , there is still an "open door" for the EuroLeague to negotiate with the NBA and FIBA, meaning the merger remains a possibility.

Windhorst added that the EuroLeague's initial rejection of a merger was due to the belief among EuroLeague owners that the NBA and FIBA undervalued the league.

Despite that, one of the EuroLeague's top teams, FC Barcelona, has gone on record as saying that talks between the EuroLeague and both the NBA and FIBA aren't necessarily dead.

In a statement provided to Jerome Pugmire of the Associated Press, Barcelona noted, "Should that proposal be amended in the future, the clubs and the EuroLeague will reconsider it."

According to Pugmire, there are currently 13 shareholder members in the EuroLeague and 20 teams overall, but the NBA wants a 16-team league.

It was also reported by L'Equipe (h/t Pugmire) that the NBA offered to pay "each future member 400 million euros ($448 million)."

Despite the EuroLeague's rejection, the NBA could launch its European league as early as 2027, with Windhorst noting that the NBA is fielding expansion offers and interest from existing teams as well.

Before the EuroLeague's official vote this week, EuroLeague Basketball CEO Chus Bueno told reporters that the EuroLeague planned to "compete" with NBA Europe if a deal is not struck.

While every indication is that an alliance is still possible, the potential for dueling professional basketball leagues in Europe exists as well.

articles.title: Peyton Manning's freshman son gets rocked, but fans are more stunned at all the scholarship offers
articles.summary: Peyton Manning's son Marshall Manning already has four Division I offers as a freshman QB, including Miami and Ohio State, despite limited playing time.
articles.body: All aboard the Marshall Manning hype train! Sure, it won't arrive until 2030, but we're getting a head start just in case there's any traffic along the way. While one Manning is about to leave college football for the NFL, the next in line is already waiting in the shadows. Yep. You read that right. Peyton Manning's son is slowly making his way onto the field for Baylor School (Chattanooga) — one of the top football programs in the country. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! I've written about Manning before this season, way back in Week 1 when he saw the field, briefly, in the season-opener. It's been pretty quiet on the Manning front since, but the freshman started bubbling back up last weekend ... for multiple different reasons. For starters, he did see some legit playing time in Baylor's blowout win over McCallie, playing all of the fourth quarter in mop-up duty. the freshman played well, completing a couple passes, leading a scoring drive, and getting his bell rung along the way. This is how you step into a throw, folks: That's not all Marshall Manning did last Friday BOOM! Good hit, better throw. I can still remember Peyton Manning getting his doors blown off and still, somehow, dropping pass after pass right in the bucket. It was amazing. Like father, like son! TEXAS OPENS SEASON AGAINST TEXAS STATE AS ARCH MANNING FACES A MAKE-OR-BREAK COLLEGE FOOTBALL YEAR Although, to be fair, Peyton would've spent 40 seconds audibling to the correct protection so he avoided that sort of hit. Marshall will learn. High school football play clocks are only so long. All in all, it was a fine night for Manning. Baylor cruised to a win, he completed some passes along the way, and finally saw some real playing time behind Ole Miss commit, Keegan Croucher. See? Nothing special, but still, some experience. That's all you want as a freshman, right? Well, that and a few scholarship offers would be nice ... Don't worry! Marshall has nothing to worry about on that front. Believe it or not, the freshman QB already has four Division I offers despite barely playing a down this season. Four! According to 247 Sports — which tracks these sort of things — Manning has already received offers from Miami, Ohio State, Purdue and Missouri State. Not bad for a 15-year-old. Not bad for a kid who hasn't even thrown his first high school touchdown yet! CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE What a time to be alive. Look, obviously it has a little something to do with his last name. We saw that with Arch Manning's insane recruitment as well. If your last name is Manning, teams are probably gonna be more willing to take a chance on you. Rightfully so. But we also live in a new age of college football. The NIL era. The transfer portal era. This ain't the world I grew up in. It's certainly not the world Peyton or Eli grew up in. Teams like Miami and Ohio State have all the money in the world to throw at these kids ... for now. We'll see how this new bill from congress shakes things up when it finally passes in 2040 (roughly). CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Why not make him an offer during his freshman season just to get on the board? You know you'll have the money when the time actually comes to be serious about it, so what's the harm? Not sure little 'ol Missouri State's gonna be able to compete with the boosters in Columbus, but I do appreciate the effort. Regardless, none of this really matters until 2030. We've still got a lot of Marshall Manning recruiting in front of us, folks. A lot. Frankly, we're just getting started.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark joins Pat McAfee on ESPN's 'College GameDay,' and left-wing podcasters have a problem with it
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark's return to Iowa for "College GameDay" drew record October ratings, but two podcast hosts questioned her appearance with Pat McAfee.
articles.body: Caitlin Clark went back to Iowa on Saturday to promote her new Nike shoe and make picks on ESPN’s "College GameDay." The show drew its biggest audience of the season and the biggest October audience in its 40-season history. Over at "The Sports Gossip Show," a podcast hosted by two women named Charlotte Wilder and Madeline Hill, the hosts found reasons to question the appearance, including Clark sitting alongside Pat McAfee. I wrote about their show in August after they mocked Riley Gaines and called Sophie Cunningham’s defense of women’s sports a "right-wing grift." So, you have a good idea of where they stand politically. Their podcast was distributed by the New York Times-owned Athletic for about a year before they announced their departure in August. Left-wing outlet Awful Announcing described their departure as part of a "broader exodus of podcast stars" from the New York Times. I must have missed the part where these two became stars. CAITLIN CLARK IS MISSING FROM ESPN' S NEW WNBA DOCUMENTARY AND THE FILMMAKERS WON' T SAY WHY On the episode, Wilder suggested Caitlin Clark needed to do something "for her own PR." So, Clark got a national platform to promote her shoe, helped drive millions of viewers to the show, and she should be concerned about her PR? I think she’ll be OK. Wilder knows the McAfee context and leaves it out anyway "Pat McAfee, in 2024, called Caitlin a ‘white b---.’ Which I could give you the context for, but it doesn’t really matter," Wilder said during the episode. Members of the media often leave out context that hurts their narrative, but they’re not usually so upfront about it. I guess it's refreshing that Wilder admits she's willing to eschew basic journalistic ethics for the sake of the story she prefers to tell. I happen to think the context does matter, so here it is. McAfee did call Clark a "white b—-" during his show in 2024 but he was defending Clark. His argument was that people needed to stop crediting the entire rookie class for attention that she was bringing to the WNBA. He was also pushing back on the suggestion that fans liked her simply because she was white. He wanted people to acknowledge how good she was and what she was doing for the league. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! McAfee apologized for his wording, explained that he meant it as a compliment and said Clark accepted his apology. Wilder acknowledged that McAfee had apologized. The podcast host stopped short of saying Clark shouldn’t have done "GameDay," but still questioned her decision to share a stage with McAfee. Clark is allowed to decide she’s comfortable with him. Why does she need to answer to two podcast hosts about an apology she reportedly accepted over two years ago? How many times does Clark have to say it? Wilder not only wants Clark to answer for appearances on GameDay, but also wants her to keep addressing something she's addressed multiple times. "We’ve just said before, if you and I were in a situation where a bunch of Black women were getting death threats and having a really hard time because of people who said they were fans of ours, I think we would say, ‘You are not a fan of mine if you are perpetuating this behavior and these actions.’ It’s not the hardest thing in the world to say," Wilder said, arguing that Clark should say "something a little more forceful." Here’s Clark in September 2024: "Nobody in our league should be facing any sort of racism, hurtful, disrespectful, hateful comments and threats," she said. "Those aren’t fans, those are trolls." And in May 2025, here's Clark responding to a question about an alleged racist incident at a Fever game (the claim was never substantiated): "There’s no place for that in our game, there’s no place for that in society." And then again in July 2026: "Harassment, hate, none of that is OK." Does she need to open every news conference with it, or would once a week satisfy these two? Wilder even acknowledged Clark had spoken out before, but reduced her comments to a general call for everyone to be treated the same. Clark explicitly condemned racism and threats and said, "Those aren’t fans, those are trolls." Wilder sure does love leaving out important context, huh? And why does Clark have to keep answering for online trolls in the first place? Random people on the internet don't get to make Clark their spokesperson just by calling themselves fans of hers. Their discussion also included Kelsey Mitchell’s complaints about the scrutiny surrounding the Fever. I wrote about those comments Sunday, and the benefits of all that attention belong in the conversation. WNBA SUDDENLY WANTS TO STICK TO BASKETBALL AFTER YEARS OF MAKING POLITICS PART OF THE PRODUCT Mitchell earned $1.4 million in WNBA salary this season, according to Spotrac. That’s more than the roughly $1.12 million she earned in her first eight seasons combined. Her play earned her the contract but Clark helped grow the audience for a league that can now pay players that kind of money. That’s a substantial contribution to her fellow players, many of whom are the Black women who Wilder and Hill think Clark needs to spend more time protecting. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE Caitlin Clark needs better PR? Seriously? "I do think she could do something at the very least for her own PR," Wilder said. Of all the things Wilder said that were outrageous, this might have been the most outlandish. Caitlin Clark is the most popular female athlete on the planet. Fever games draw more viewers than any other team in the WNBA. Clark is a spokesperson for major brands like State Farm and Gatorade. Her first signature Nike shoe nearly sold out on Nike’s website within two hours of its release. So what, exactly, does Clark need to do differently? Bow down to the left-wing media mob to appease podcasters like Wilder and Hill? Saturday’s "GameDay" averaged 2.9 million viewers, according to ESPN. It was the most-watched episode of the season and the most-watched October episode in the show’s history. The final hour, in which Clark appeared, averaged 3.7 million viewers. For the record, "The Sports Gossip Show" averaged about 7,200 YouTube views across 39 episodes spanning roughly five months. If anyone needs some PR advice, it's these two. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD Although, I’d love to hear the pitch to Clark’s PR team after that weekend. "Sorry about all the people watching your client promote her shoe. Have you considered getting her to issue another statement about racism? There's this podcast that no one watches that would really appreciate it. Thanks."

articles.title: El 'nuevo' MVP de la Euroliga se moja: el Madrid, candidato, con Barcelona y Valencia en media tabla
articles.standfirst: Elijah Bryant predice cómo quedará la nueva temporada europea y coloca a los blancos en la parte alta de la clasificación, con blaugranas y taronjas en la zona media y vitorianos a la cola
articles.summary: Elijah Bryant predice cómo quedará la nueva temporada europea y coloca a los blancos en la parte alta de la clasificación, con blaugranas y taronjas en la zona media y vitorianos a la cola
articles.body: La Euroliga 2026-27 ya ha echado a andar en una temporada que vuelve a prometer emociones fuertes. En un inicio prometedor para unos y dubitativo para otros, ha sido el MVP de las últimas dos jornadas, Elijah Bryant, el que se ha atrevido a hacer sus pronósticos para esta campaña de la mejor competición continental. A través de su canal de YouTube, el jugador de Hapoel Tel Aviv ha colocado en un ranking con cinco escalones diferentes a los 20 equipos que conforman la Euroliga este año. Según el criterio del escolta, los cuatro conjuntos españoles quedan ubicados en distintos rangos con aspiraciones dispares. El primero que aparece en su tabla es el Real Madrid. Pese a que el equipo de Pedro Martínez ha arrancado 0-3 con su peor inicio histórico en la Copa de Europa, Bryant sitúa a los blancos en la quinta posición, en un puesto que podría intuirse como candidato a levantar el trofeo a final de temporada. Respecto a los otros españoles, Elijah coloca a Barcelona y Valencia en un tren de equipos de la zona media. El estadounidense duda si poner al nuevo proyecto de Sekulic en el tercer escalón pero finalmente acompaña en el cuarto a conjuntos como Partizán, Milán, Maccabi o Besiktas, donde también se encuentra la remodelada plantilla taronja que ha heredado Xavi Albert en el Roig Arena. Para el quinto y último peldaño, Bryant considera a Baskonia como uno de los últimos de la tabla. El que fuera campeón de la NBA con los Milwaukee Bucks en 2021 ordenó como máximos favoritos para ganar la Euroliga al Hapoel, su club, seguido de los dos griegos, Panathinaikos y Olympiacos. Por detrás, en un segundo escalón, quedarían Fenerbahce y Real Madrid. Los siguientes tres que les siguen serían, bajo su criterio, Estrella Roja, Dubai y Anadolu Efes, con Barcelona y el Partizán de Joan Peñarroya cerrando los puestos que dan acceso al play-in. En una liga en la que predomina el acento español en los banquillos, Elijah Bryant se detuvo a analizar detalles de algunos de ellos. Sobre el Estrella Roja de Ibon Navarro comentó que es muy difícil ganar en Belgrado por la presión de los aficionados, mientras que del Anadolu Efes de Pablo Laso opina que pueden ser una segunda versión de Mónaco pese a la pérdida de su gran capitán, Shane Larkin. En cuanto al Dubai de Xavi Pascual, Bryant destaca que son un "gran equipo" pero que "sólo hay un balón", en una plantilla que cuenta con jugadores como Shengelia, Okobo, Musa o Bacon, por lo que está expectante de cómo pueden encontrar cada uno ese rol en la pista para el funcionamiento del grupo a ganar. Por último, también tuvo palabras para figuras como Obradovic o Tony Parker. Sobre el mítico base galo y técnico de ASVEL dice que "fue genial", pero eso no evita que coloque a los franceses en la parte baja. Respecto al legendario entrenador serbio de Panathinaikos cree que "si hay alguien que puede hacer funcionar a todas esas estrellas, es él". Cabe recordar que Elijah Bryant ha sido elegido mejor jugador de las jornadas 2 y 3 de la Euroliga, con ambos dobles dobles en los encuentros ante Estrella Roja y Real Madrid, cuando firmó un partidazo de 22 puntos, 13 rebotes y 7 asistencias en la victoria (102-98) ante los de Pedro Martínez. Ya sólo queda esperar unos meses y ver si los triples que anota en pista se trasladan a los que se ha tirado con sus predicciones...

articles.title: NHL Insider Drops Surprising Update on Simon Edvinsson’s Future With Red Wings
articles.summary: Darren Dreger reveals Simon Edvinsson may still be willing to stay with the Detroit Red Wings despite ongoing contract disputes and trade rumors.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings may not have lost Simon Edvinsson just yet, despite recent reports that the young defenseman would prefer to be traded. NHL insider Darren Dreger has provided an encouraging update on Edvinsson's willingness to remain in Detroit, offering some hope in a contract dispute that has quickly become one of the organization's biggest concerns.

Edvinsson remains unsigned as a restricted free agent, and frustration surrounding negotiations has reportedly contributed to his return to Sweden. However, the latest reporting suggests that while the relationship between the two sides has been strained, there may still be an opportunity to repair it.

Apr 7, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson (77) passes in the first period against the Columbus Blue Jackets at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

Darren Dreger Offers Encouraging Simon Edvinsson Update

According to Jake Tye of The Hockey News , Dreger revealed during an appearance on TSN's First Up that Edvinsson remains "very much open to the idea of staying in Detroit." Dreger also indicated that the Red Wings remain committed to bringing Edvinsson back, although any agreement would need to make financial sense for the 23-year-old defenseman.

That is encouraging news for Detroit, especially considering how quickly the situation appeared to deteriorate over the past week. Edvinsson had reportedly become so frustrated with the negotiating process that leaving the organization emerged as his preferred outcome.

As we previously reported , Sportsnet insider Elliotte Friedman revealed on October 3 that Edvinsson preferred a trade rather than continuing his career with the Red Wings. That development raised serious questions about whether Detroit could salvage its relationship with a player widely viewed as a cornerstone of the franchise's future.

However, there is an important distinction between being frustrated with contract negotiations and being completely unwilling to remain with an organization. Dreger's comments suggest Edvinsson may still be receptive to staying in Hockeytown if the Red Wings can present an agreement that meets his expectations.

Red Wings Contract Negotiations Have Created Frustration

One of the more concerning aspects of the Edvinsson situation involves how long the organization reportedly waited before making its first contract offer. According to TSN insider Pierre LeBrun, Detroit did not present Edvinsson with an initial proposal until approximately September 17, leaving the restricted free agent waiting for much of the offseason.

For a player expected to become a foundational piece of the Red Wings' defense, that timeline raises legitimate questions about how negotiations were handled. Edvinsson previously expressed interest in remaining with Detroit long term, making the deterioration of the relationship particularly frustrating for an organization already dealing with uncertainty elsewhere on its roster.

There have been indications that Detroit is attempting to correct course, including a willingness to consider different contract structures. As we reported earlier this week , the Red Wings have reportedly moved away from their initial preference for a shorter bridge agreement and presented longer-term offers in an effort to reach a deal.

That adjustment could prove important because it suggests Detroit understands the urgency of securing Edvinsson's future. However, changing the length of a proposed contract does not automatically resolve disagreements over salary, and there is still considerable work to be done before anyone should expect an agreement.

Latest Reporting Suggests a Deal Is Still Far From Guaranteed

While Dreger's earlier comments provided optimism, his subsequent reporting makes it clear that the two sides have not yet reached a breakthrough. According to an October 7 NHL Rumors report detailing Dreger's latest update , Detroit remains in contact with Edvinsson's agent, J.P. Barry, but negotiations have not produced meaningful progress.

The Red Wings are also reportedly listening to inquiries from other NHL teams as they evaluate their options. That does not mean Detroit has decided to trade Edvinsson, but it indicates that interim general manager Shawn Horcoff is weighing the potential return against the cost of signing the defenseman.

For Detroit, that creates a difficult balancing act because Edvinsson is exactly the type of young player the organization should be building around. Trading him could produce valuable assets, but finding another defenseman with his combination of size, skating ability, and long-term potential would be no easy task.

There is also a significant difference between exploring trade interest and actively shopping a player. Until the Red Wings determine that negotiations cannot be salvaged, keeping Edvinsson in Detroit remains a realistic possibility.

Why Keeping Simon Edvinsson Matters So Much

Edvinsson recorded nine goals and 16 assists for 25 points in 72 games during the 2025-26 season, continuing to establish himself as a significant part of Detroit's defensive corps. His size, mobility, and ability to handle difficult assignments make him more valuable than his offensive numbers alone might suggest.

Alongside Moritz Seider, Edvinsson was expected to help anchor the Red Wings' blue line for years to come. Losing him at just 23 years old would create another substantial hole for a franchise that has spent the past decade attempting to build a roster capable of returning to the Stanley Cup Playoffs.

Detroit also has to consider the message another high-profile departure would send about the organization's direction. With Dylan Larkin's future uncertain and the Red Wings already facing increased pressure to deliver results, retaining an important young player such as Edvinsson would provide some much-needed stability.

That is why Dreger's update matters beyond the immediate contract negotiations. If Edvinsson remains willing to stay, Detroit still has an opportunity to retain one of its most valuable young assets rather than being forced to consider a trade that could dramatically reshape its defensive corps.

Mar 28, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; Detroit Red Wings defenseman Simon Edvinsson (77) skates with the puck in the first period against the Philadelphia Flyers at Little Caesars Arena. Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)

The Door Is Still Open, But Detroit Must Act

The Simon Edvinsson situation remains unresolved, but the latest insider reporting provides reason to believe his days with the Detroit Red Wings are not necessarily numbered. Despite the frustration, trade speculation, and continued absence of a contract, Dreger's comments suggest Edvinsson could still be convinced to remain in Hockeytown.

However, Detroit cannot afford to mistake that willingness for a guarantee that an agreement will eventually be reached. The Red Wings must find a way to bridge the remaining differences before the situation deteriorates further and a potentially avoidable trade becomes a more realistic outcome.

For now, the door remains open for Simon Edvinsson to stay with the Red Wings. Whether he actually walks back through it will depend on what happens at the negotiating table.

articles.title: Breanna Stewart and WNBA refs at odds amid reset timeout controversy in Liberty's loss to Dream
articles.summary: A bizarre ending to the playoffs' single best game.
articles.body:
With 4.3 seconds to game in Game 2 of the WNBA semifinals, the New York Liberty -- according to ESPN's scorebug -- had a reset timeout they could have used to advance the ball and have a genuine shot to tie a back-and-forth game against the Atlanta Dream .

Down three, the Liberty chose not to call this timeout, which left Stewart to heave a Hail Mary toward the Dream basket. The shot never had a chance.

The big story coming out of the Liberty's 101-98 overtime loss to the Dream at State Farm Arena on Wednesday centers on whether New York actually did have a chance to move the ball up for a sideline out-of-bounds play.

Stewart and Liberty coach Chris DeMarco were adamant postgame that the refereeing crew told them New York was out of reset timeouts . So Stewart was pretty surprised when, as she told reporters, she discovered there was indeed one reset timeout remaining.

"When I ask both refs if we have a reset timeout at the end, and they tell us 'no', and then we leave the game with the reset timeout, it's pretty frustrating," Stewart said.

Stewart was brilliant on Wednesday. It's no wonder the loss stings more painfully for her. She scored 25 points in the first half. In all, she scored 35 points, hauled in 11 rebounds and dished out six assists. It was one of the finest postseason performances in a decorated career that has glittered with huge displays on big stages.

Now down 2-0 in the best-of-five series, the Liberty has no margin for error. But according to the referees' pool report early Thursday morning, New York messed up at the end of Game 2.

The officiating crew contends the Liberty did have one more reset timeout: the same reset timeout it was awarded when overtime began, alongside two standard team timeouts.

"Stewart was standing behind Referee (Kevin) Fahy when he confirmed with his partner, between (Angel) Reese's penalty free throws, that New York did indeed have a reset timeout remaining," crew chief Fatou Cissoko-Stephens said.

The natural conclusion to draw is that someone here is lying.

The referees maintain New York had a reset timeout it consciously chose not to use. Stewart and DeMarco claim they were told explicitly that there was no reset timeout, that the ESPN scorebug was not to be believed.

The controversy can be interpreted as an embittered response from the Liberty to a game they should have won. Marine Fauthoux, a sparingly-used rookie, scored a career-high 20 points and drilled four 3-pointers -- including the one that took the game to overtime. New York shot 55 percent from the field, and a few breaks the other way would have seen this series all tied up.

But just as the referees did not compel Fauthoux to have a career night, the referees didn't ask the Liberty to miss seven free throws, nor to turn the ball over 16 times. They didn't ask Sabrina Ionescu to send a hook pass into the crowd on New York's penultimate overtime possession.

There are plenty of legitimate criticisms over the state of WNBA officiating. But the Liberty coaching staff -- helmed by the first-year coach DeMarco -- was responsible for keeping track of how many timeouts were left and clearly communicating that information to Stewart and her teammates.

The communication breakdown could well cost the Liberty a chance to play in the WNBA Finals for the third time in four seasons.

articles.title: Liberty's Breanna Stewart Calls Out Refs After Unused Timeout in Loss to Dream, 'Pretty Frustrating'
articles.summary: New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart voiced her frustration with the officiating toward the end of Wednesday's 101-98 WNBA semifinals loss to the Atlanta Dream.
articles.body:
New York Liberty star Breanna Stewart voiced her frustration with the officiating toward the end of Wednesday's 101-98 WNBA semifinals loss to the Atlanta Dream.

The Dream's Angel Reese sank a pair of free throws to put the Dream up by three with 4.3 seconds remaining in overtime. New York opted against using its reset timeout, and Stewart had to settle for a long-range heave in the waning moments.

The two-time MVP said in her postgame press conference the referees told her the Liberty didn't have a reset timeout, hence their inbounding the ball from beneath Atlanta's basket:

Liberty coach Chris DeMarco echoed Stewart's account.

Fatou Cissoko-Stephens, the game's lead official, pushed back on that narrative.

"Stewart was standing behind referee (Kevin) Fahy when he confirmed with his (officiating) partner between Reese's penalty free throws that the Liberty did indeed have a reset (timeout) remaining," she said, per The Athletic's Annie Costabile .

DeMarco and his staff wouldn't have been able to draw up a final play if the Liberty had used their reset timeout. Under that rule , teams are allowed to advance the ball and make substitutions, but they can't huddle along the bench.

At the very least, New York wouldn't have had to waste valuable time getting the ball across half-court.

Costabile reported the Liberty lodged a formal inquiry with the league. Even if that works out in the team's favor, it will only bring so much satisfaction when the result is final.

New York trails 0-2 with the series heading to Barclays Center for Game 3 on Friday.

articles.title: SGA Defends Chet Holmgren, Says 'I Carry A Lot of the Weight' for Thunder's G7 Loss to Spurs
articles.summary: Despite Chet Holmgren receiving the bulk of the criticism for the Oklahoma City Thunder's playoff loss to the San Antonio Spurs, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander wants to shoulder the blame for what happened in the series.
articles.body:
Despite Chet Holmgren receiving the bulk of the criticism for the Oklahoma City Thunder's playoff loss to the San Antonio Spurs, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander wants to shoulder the blame for what happened in the series.

Speaking to Sean Gregory of TIME , Gilgeous-Alexander explained "I carry a lot of the weight" for the Thunder losing to the Spurs as part of his defense for Holmgren.

"I don't think it's on Chet," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "I carry a lot of the weight. The only way you can truly fail is if you don't learn from the moment. I know the type of guy he is. And I know what type of worker he is. He'll definitely do it."

Broadcaster sorry for false LeBron rumor

Holmgren's postseason was going fine until the Western Conference Finals. He averaged 18.6 points on 60.0 percent shooting (38.7 percent from three) and 9.1 rebounds per game in eight starts through the first two rounds.

Taking on the Spurs and frequently matched up with Victor Wembanyama on both ends of the floor greatly diminished Holmgren's output. He averaged 10.7 points on 51.0 percent shooting (27.3 percent from three) and 7.1 rebounds per contest in seven games.

Game 7, in particular, was brutal for Holmgren with four points and two field-goal attempts in 33 minutes. The performance even drew comparisons to Ben Simmons' infamous Game 7 against the Atlanta Hawks in 2021.

There was even some speculation that Oklahoma City might look to trade Holmgren one year after giving him a five-year max extension , though that was quickly debunked .

Gilgeous-Alexander did all he could to help the Thunder in Game 7 after struggling for most of the series up to that point. He had 35 points on 12-of-21 shooting and nine assists, but the Spurs earned a 111-103 win to end Oklahoma City's quest for a repeat.

Despite an ugly finish to the season, Holmgren made his first All-Star team and finished second in Defensive Player of the Year voting as a 23-year-old. He has earned some leeway to remind everyone why his max extension after the 2024-25 season wasn't even a question for the Thunder.

The NBA schedule-makers have given Holmgren a chance to redeem himself at the start of the 2026-27 season since the Thunder and Spurs will play on opening night on Oct. 20.
